areas.name: Matrix analysis toolkit
areas.summary: Deterministic facts every RandNLA proof reaches for: SVD, best low-rank approximation, perturbation, projections, pseudoinverse, trace inequalities, the Loewner order.

areas.name: Trace inequalities and the Loewner order
Gaussian and random matrix facts
areas.summary: What a standard Gaussian matrix does: invariance, moments, inverse moments of the pseudoinverse, extreme singular values. The bottleneck for every Gaussian-sketch argument.

areas.name: Concentration inequalities
areas.summary: Scalar and matrix tail bounds. The matrix side is done (Tropp Ch. 3–8); the scalar side is scattered across Mathlib and external libraries.

areas.name: Sketching primitives
areas.summary: Johnson–Lindenstrauss, subspace embeddings, approximate matrix multiplication, leverage-score sampling. The vocabulary in which randomized algorithms are analysed.

areas.name: Low-rank approximation
areas.summary: Deterministic structural lemmas (projection error, truncation, power iteration, Nyström) and the randomized algorithm guarantees that consume them.

areas.name: Trace, diagonal and quadratic-form estimation
areas.summary: Hutchinson-type estimators, their variance and tails; randomized Krylov estimators (random-start power and Lanczos, stochastic Lanczos quadrature). Small statements with very high reuse.

areas.name: Krylov methods
areas.summary: Krylov subspaces, Lanczos, conjugate gradient, Gauss quadrature and the spectral measure: deterministic theory resting on the matrix and polynomial layers. Randomized Krylov guarantees (random-start Lanczos, block Krylov, SLQ) sit with their consumers in low-rank approximation and estimation.

areas.name: Randomized solvers (consumers)
areas.summary: Sketch-and-solve, sketch-and-precondition, Kaczmarz and sketch-and-project. Mostly consumers of sketching and matrix facts; Kaczmarz is itself a clean foundation.

areas.name: Gaussian measure: log-Sobolev and comparison
areas.summary: The machinery behind Gaussian concentration and Gordon's theorem: integration by parts, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup, log-Sobolev, Herbst, Slepian and Sudakov–Fernique.

areas.name: Polynomial approximation
areas.summary: Chebyshev polynomials and their extremal properties, Markov-type derivative bounds, interpolation. Layer 0, no matrices: the deterministic polynomial facts that Krylov, Lanczos, CG and block Krylov rates reduce to.

areas.name: Chebyshev polynomials
areas.summary: Growth outside [-1,1], second kind, extremal and minimax properties, monic minimality.

areas.name: Approximation, derivatives, interpolation
areas.summary: Gap-amplifying polynomials, approximation of 1/x, Markov and Bernstein inequalities, Lagrange remainder and Chebyshev interpolation.

areas.name: Krylov bases: grade, Arnoldi and Lanczos relations
areas.title: Krylov bases: grade, Arnoldi and Lanczos relations
areas.summary: Dimension of Krylov spaces, the Arnoldi relation and its Hessenberg matrix, exactness of Krylov projection on polynomials, block Krylov spaces.

areas.name: Polynomial methods for linear systems
areas.title: Polynomial methods for linear systems
areas.summary: Residual polynomials; GMRES, MINRES, FOM, preconditioned CG, CGLS/LSQR, Chebyshev iteration and Richardson, with their spectral convergence bounds.

areas.name: Field of values and non-normal GMRES theory
areas.title: Field of values and non-normal GMRES theory
areas.summary: Numerical range, Crouzeix–Palencia, the Elman / Beckermann–Goreinov–Tyrtyshnikov bounds and the Greenbaum–Pták–Strakoš caution.

areas.name: Krylov approximation of f(A)b
areas.title: Krylov approximation of f(A)b
areas.summary: Lanczos-FA and Arnoldi-FA: the Krylov approximation of a matrix function times a vector is within twice (Hermitian) or 2(1+√2) times (general) the best polynomial approximation error.

areas.name: Ritz values and eigenvector angles
areas.title: Ritz values and eigenvector angles
areas.summary: Gap-dependent Kaniel–Paige–Saad theory: the angle between an eigenvector and the Krylov space, and the Ritz value error.

areas.name: Chebyshev series and analytic approximation
areas.title: Chebyshev series and analytic approximation
areas.summary: Chebyshev coefficients, Bernstein ellipses, aliasing, and the ATAP convergence theorems (3.1, 4.1–4.2, 7.1–7.2, 8.1–8.2).

areas.name: Best approximation, Jackson and Lebesgue constants
areas.title: Best approximation, Jackson and Lebesgue constants
areas.summary: E_n(f), equioscillation and de la Vallée Poussin, Jackson's theorem, Lebesgue constants of interpolation.

areas.name: Approximating specific functions, with lower bounds
areas.title: Approximating specific functions, with lower bounds
areas.summary: x^s, e^{-x}, x^{-1/2}, log x, sign(x) with explicit degrees, and the matching degree lower bounds (1/x, e^{-x}, sign).

areas.name: Majorization, Ky Fan and unitarily invariant norms
areas.title: Majorization, Ky Fan and unitarily invariant norms
areas.summary: Majorization of spectra, Ky Fan / Schatten / unitarily invariant norms, and the eigenvalue and singular-value inequalities stated with them (Ky Fan, Schur–Horn, Lidskii, Horn).

areas.name: Subspace angles and sin θ theorems
areas.title: Subspace angles and sin θ theorems
areas.summary: Canonical angles between subspaces and the Davis–Kahan / Wedin perturbation bounds for eigen- and singular subspaces.

areas.name: Inverses, conditioning and factorizations
areas.title: Inverses, conditioning and factorizations
areas.summary: Neumann series and inverse perturbation, condition numbers, forward-error bounds for linear systems and least squares, Cholesky and QR as existence-and-uniqueness statements.

results.title: Frobenius and spectral norms: mixed inequalities
results.informal: Submultiplicativity: $\|AB\|_F \le \|A\|\,\|B\|_F$ and $\|AB\|_F \le \|A\|_F\,\|B\|$. Norm comparison: $\|A\| \le \|A\|_F \le \sqrt{\operatorname{rank}(A)}\,\|A\|$. Both norms are unitarily invariant, and $$\|A\|_F^2 = \operatorname{tr}(A^\top A) = \sum_i \sigma_i^2.$$

results.title: Singular value decomposition of a matrix
results.informal: Every $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ factors as $A = U\Sigma V^\top$ with $U, V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ diagonal with $\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_{\min(m,n)} \ge 0$. Splitting at rank $k$ gives the block form $$A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top.$$
results.conclusion: $A = U\Sigma V^\top$ with $U, V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ diagonal with $\sigma_1 \ge \dots \ge \sigma_{\min(m,n)} \ge 0$; at rank $k$, $A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$

formalizations.usage: For any `A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ`, `obtain ⟨U, V, h⟩ := exists_isSVD A` gives `h : IsSVD A U V` (orthogonal `U`, `V` and `A = U * rectDiag (singularValues A) * Vᵀ`); no hypotheses.
formalizations.note: IsSVD A U V: Uᵀ U = 1, Vᵀ V = 1, A = U · rectDiag (singularValues A) · Vᵀ, where singularValues A : ℕ → ℝ is Mathlib's LinearMap.singularValues of toEuclideanLin A (zero-indexed, antitone, zero beyond the rank). Also uniqueness of σ, block split at k (IsSVD.eq_head_add_tail), AᵀA and AAᵀ diagonalisations, frobSq = Σσ², invariance under orthogonal factors and transpose.

formalizations.usage: From `h : IsSVD A U V` and a split index `k`; rewrites `A` as the head `U * rectDiag (σ masked to i < k) * Vᵀ` (the truncated SVD) plus the tail `U * rectDiag (σ masked to i ≥ k) * Vᵀ`.
No hypotheses; gives `frobSq A = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (min m n), singularValues A k ^ 2`.
Pass `hU : Uᵀ * U = 1`, `hV : Vᵀ * V = 1`, `τ` nonnegative (`hτ0`) and antitone (`hτ`), and `hA : A = U * rectDiag τ * Vᵀ`; gives `singularValues A k = τ k` for every `k < min m n`.

results.title: Eckart–Young–Mirsky: best rank-k approximation
results.informal: Both minima are attained by the truncated SVD $\lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k$: $$\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\| = \sigma_{k+1}(A), \qquad \min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\|_F^2 = \sum_{i>k} \sigma_i^2.$$
results.conclusion: $\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\| = \sigma_{k+1}(A)$ and $\min_{\operatorname{rank} B \le k} \|A - B\|_F^2 = \sum_{i>k} \sigma_i^2$, both attained by $\lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k$

formalizations.usage: `specNorm (A - truncatedSVD A k) = singularValues A k` (attainment).

results.notes: The extension proves the Frobenius minimum, attained by its actual truncated SVD, for every target rank and shape. The spectral-norm minimum remains a separate open component; this combined entry is not promoted by the Frobenius proof. results.title: Weyl and Mirsky perturbation bounds for singular values
results.informal: For every $i$, $|\sigma_i(A+E) - \sigma_i(A)| \le \|E\|$, and $$\Big(\sum_i \big(\sigma_i(A+E) - \sigma_i(A)\big)^2\Big)^{1/2} \le \|E\|_F.$$

results.title: Courant–Fischer min-max and Rayleigh quotients
results.informal: For Hermitian $A$, $$\lambda_k(A) = \max_{\dim S = k}\ \min_{x \in S,\ \|x\|=1} x^\top A x.$$ In particular $\lambda_{\max}$ is the sup of the Rayleigh quotient and $\lambda_{\min}$ the inf.
results.conclusion: $\lambda_k(A) = \max_{\dim S = k}\ \min_{x \in S,\ \|x\|=1} x^\top A x$; in particular $\lambda_{\max} = \sup_{\|x\|=1} x^\top Ax$ and $\lambda_{\min} = \inf_{\|x\|=1} x^\top Ax$

results.title: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse and its identities
results.informal: The general real Moore–Penrose inverse exists at every rank, is unique, and satisfies all four Penrose identities. It agrees with pinvL/pinvR when the respective Gram matrix is invertible. Its products are the orthogonal range projectors. Its norm is zero for the zero matrix and otherwise the reciprocal of the smallest positive singular value. For every A, $\|A^\dagger\|_F^2=\operatorname{tr}((AA^\top)^\dagger)$.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, over arbitrary finite index types
Full-column or full-row rank is required only for the ordinary inverse formulas
results.conclusion: $AA^\dagger A=A$, $A^\dagger AA^\dagger=A^\dagger$, $(AA^\dagger)^\top=AA^\dagger$, $(A^\dagger A)^\top=A^\dagger A$; the inverse is unique, and $\|A^\dagger\|=0$ when rank is zero, otherwise $1/\sigma_{\operatorname{rank}(A)}(A)$.

results.title: Orthogonal projectors and residuals
results.informal: For $Q$ with orthonormal columns, $P = QQ^\top$ is an orthogonal projector and $\|A\|_F^2 = \|PA\|_F^2 + \|(I-P)A\|_F^2$. If $\operatorname{range}(A\Omega) \subseteq \operatorname{range}(Q)$ then $(I-P)A\Omega = 0$. Projection error is monotone under range inclusion.

formalizations.usage: `gaussianMatrix p m : Measure (Fin p → Fin m → ℝ)` is the law of a `p × m` standard Gaussian matrix; samples are arrays, so wrap them with `Matrix.of G` for matrix algebra and state random test matrices as `Measure.map Ω μ = gaussianMatrix p m`.
Instance: gaussianMatrix p m is a Gaussian measure in Mathlib's sense (IsGaussian), with HasGaussianLaw for linear forms via linForm.

results.title: Isserlis / Wick formula for Gaussian moments
results.informal: $\mathbb{E}[g_{i_1}\cdots g_{i_{2k}}]$ is the sum over pairings of products of covariances. General engine for all polynomial moments (fourth moments, Hutchinson variance, AMM).
hypotheses: $g = (g_1, \dots, g_n)$ a centred Gaussian vector with covariance $C$
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}[g_{i_1}\cdots g_{i_{2k}}] = \sum_{\pi} \prod_{\{a,b\} \in \pi} C_{i_a i_b}$, the sum over all pairings $\pi$ of $\{1, \dots, 2k\}$
results.notes: Isserlis for degree-four products of Gaussian matrix entries and of linear forms is proved in Gaussian/Moments/FourthMoment.lean (integral_entry_mul_four_gaussianMatrix, integral_linear_mul_four_gaussianMatrix); the general pairing formula remains open.

results.title: Gaussian approximate matrix multiplication identity

results.title: Chi-square lower tail

results.informal: For independent Hermitian summands $X_k$ with $Y = \sum_k X_k$: $$\mathbb{E}\,\lambda_{\max}(Y) \le \inf_{\theta>0} \frac{1}{\theta}\log\operatorname{tr}\exp\Big(\sum_k \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{\theta X_k}\Big),$$ and the matching tail bound.

results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}\,\lambda_{\max}(Y) \le \inf_{\theta>0} \frac{1}{\theta}\log\operatorname{tr}\exp\Big(\sum_k \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{\theta X_k}\Big)$ and $\mathbb{P}[\lambda_{\max}(Y) \ge t] \le \inf_{\theta>0} e^{-\theta t}\operatorname{tr}\exp\Big(\sum_k \log\mathbb{E}\,e^{\theta X_k}\Big)$

formalizations.usage: Pass independent (`hIndep : iIndepFun X μ`), measurable, a.e.-Hermitian, integrable `X : Fin N → Ω → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ` and `hExp` (integrability of `matrixExp (θ • X k)`); for `0 < θ` gives the `lambdaMax` expectation and tail bounds in terms of `traceExp (cumulantSum μ X θ)`, and for `θ < 0` the `lambdaMin` analogues.
Pass independent, measurable, a.e.-Hermitian `X k` and `hExp` (integrability of `matrixExp (θ • X k)`); gives `∫ traceExp (∑ k, θ • X k ω) ∂μ ≤ traceExp (cumulantSum μ X θ)`.

results.title: Matrix Gaussian and Rademacher series
results.informal: $$\mathbb{E}\Big\|\sum_k \gamma_k A_k\Big\| \le \sqrt{2\sigma^2\log(d_1+d_2)}$$ with $\sigma^2 = \max\big(\|\sum_k A_kA_k^*\|, \|\sum_k A_k^* A_k\|\big)$.
hypotheses: $\gamma_k$ independent, all standard Gaussian or all Rademacher
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{E}\Big\|\sum_k \gamma_k A_k\Big\| \le \sqrt{2\sigma^2\log(d_1+d_2)}$, with the matching tail bound

formalizations.usage: Pass Hermitian `A k` (`hA`) and independent measurable scalars `g` with `hLaw` (Gaussian or Rademacher); for `Y = ∑ g k • A k` gives `v = spectralNorm (∑ A k ^ 2)`, `E lambdaMax Y ≤ √(2 v log d)` and the tail `gaussianSeriesTail d v t`.

Pass fixed `B : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ` and independent measurable scalars `g` with `hLaw` (all standard Gaussian or all Rademacher); for `Z = ∑ g k • B k` with second moment `v`, gives `v = max ‖∑ B Bᴴ‖ ‖∑ Bᴴ B‖`, `E spectralNorm Z ≤ √(2 v log(m + n))` and the tail `gaussianSeriesTail (m + n) v t`.

results.notes: Complex rectangular variance uses adjoints, not ordinary transposes.

results.title: Matrix Chernoff inequality
results.informal: Upper and lower tails for $\lambda_{\max}$ and $\lambda_{\min}$ of a sum of independent PSD matrices bounded by $L$.
hypotheses: $X_1, \dots, X_N$ independent random PSD $d\times d$ matrices
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{P}[\lambda_{\min}(Y) \le (1-\varepsilon)\mu_{\min}] \le d\Big[\frac{e^{-\varepsilon}}{(1-\varepsilon)^{1-\varepsilon}}\Big]^{\mu_{\min}/L}$ for $0 \le \varepsilon < 1$ and $\mathbb{P}[\lambda_{\max}(Y) \ge (1+\varepsilon)\mu_{\max}] \le d\Big[\frac{e^{\varepsilon}}{(1+\varepsilon)^{1+\varepsilon}}\Big]^{\mu_{\max}/L}$ for $\varepsilon \ge 0$, with matching expectation bounds

formalizations.usage: Pass independent, measurable, a.e.-Hermitian `X k` with `hBound : 0 ≤ lambdaMin (X k) ∧ lambdaMax (X k) ≤ L` a.e. and `hL : 0 ≤ L`; with `a`, `b` the extreme eigenvalues of `E ∑ X k`, gives expectation bounds for every `θ > 0`, the lower tail `chernoffLowerTail d a L ε` (`0 ≤ ε < 1`) and the upper tail `chernoffUpperTail d b L ε` (`0 ≤ ε`).

results.title: Matrix Bernstein inequality
results.informal: Tail and expectation bounds for $\|\sum_k S_k\|$ with $\|S_k\| \le L$ and matrix variance $v$.

formalizations.usage: Pass independent, centred, a.e.-Hermitian `X k` with `hL2 : MemLp (X k) 2 μ` and `hBound : lambdaMax (X k) ≤ L` a.e.; gives `v = spectralNorm (∑ E X k ^ 2)`, `E lambdaMax (∑ X k) ≤ √(2 v log d) + L log d / 3` and the tail `bernsteinTail d v L t`.

Pass independent, measurable, centred (`hMean`) `S k : Ω → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℂ` with `hBound : spectralNorm (S k) ≤ L` a.e. and `0 ≤ L`; for `Z = ∑ S k` and `v = rectSecondMoment μ Z` gives the formula for `v`, `E spectralNorm Z ≤ √(2 v log(m + n)) + L log(m + n) / 3` and the tail `bernsteinTail (m + n) v L t`.

results.title: Intrinsic-dimension Chernoff and Bernstein
results.informal: Replaces $\log d$ with $\log\operatorname{intdim}(V)$.
hypotheses: independent random matrices as in matrix Chernoff or Bernstein
a semidefinite upper bound $V$ on $\mathbb{E}Y$ (Chernoff) or on the matrix variance (Bernstein)
results.conclusion: the matrix Chernoff and Bernstein bounds hold with the ambient dimension replaced by $\operatorname{intdim}(V)$, e.g. $\mathbb{P}[\|Z\| \ge t] \le 4\operatorname{intdim}(V)\exp\Big(\frac{-t^2/2}{v + Lt/3}\Big)$ for $t \ge \sqrt{v} + L/3$

formalizations.usage: Pass independent centred `S k` with `spectralNorm (S k) ≤ L` a.e. and variance proxies `V₁`, `V₂` (not both 0) with `loewnerLE (E Z Zᴴ) V₁` and `loewnerLE (E Zᴴ Z) V₂`; with `r = intrinsicDimension (fromBlocks V₁ 0 0 V₂)` and `v = max ‖V₁‖ ‖V₂‖`, gives `P[t ≤ spectralNorm Z] ≤ 4 r exp(−(t²/2)/(v + L t/3))` for `t ≥ √v + L/3`.

Pass independent PSD `X k` with `lambdaMax (X k) ≤ L` a.e. (`0 < L`) and a nonzero `M` with `hMeanBound : loewnerLE (E ∑ X k) M`; with `r = intrinsicDimension M`, `a = lambdaMax M`, gives `E lambdaMax ≤ (e^θ − 1)/θ · a + (L/θ) log(2r)` for `θ > 0` and the tail `2 r exp((a/L)(ε − (1+ε) log(1+ε)))` for `ε ≥ L/a`.

results.title: Sampling lemma: sums of independent rank-one PSD samples
results.informal: If the $x_j$ are i.i.d. with $\mathbb{E}\,x_jx_j^\top = I$ and $\|x_j\|^2 \le L$ a.s., then $\frac{1}{k}\sum_j x_jx_j^\top$ has eigenvalues in $[1-\varepsilon, 1+\varepsilon]$ with probability at least $1 - 2d\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/(cL))$. The one corollary of matrix Chernoff that every sampling-based embedding uses.
results.conclusion: $\mathbb{P}\big[\lambda_{\min}\big(\tfrac1N\sum_k M_k\big) \le 1-\varepsilon\big] \le d\,e^{-\varepsilon^2 N/(2L)}$ and $\mathbb{P}\big[\lambda_{\max}\big(\tfrac1N\sum_k M_k\big) \ge 1+\varepsilon\big] \le d\,e^{-\varepsilon^2 N/(3L)}$ for $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$

formalizations.usage: Lower tail only.
Upper tail only.
Isotropic i.i.d. PSD summands with `λ_max ≤ L`: `P(λ_min(N⁻¹ΣM_k) ≤ 1-ε) ≤ d e^{-ε²N/(2L)}` and `P(λ_max ≥ 1+ε) ≤ d e^{-ε²N/(3L)}` for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`.

results.notes: Matrix Chernoff is proved; this packaging is cheap and unlocks SRHT, leverage-score sampling and sparsification. Constants made explicit (2 and 3) on 2026-10-10.

results.title: Matrix Freedman / martingale Bernstein
results.informal: Martingale version of matrix Bernstein; used for adaptive sampling and streaming.
hypotheses: $Y_k = \sum_{j \le k} X_j$ a Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix martingale with $\lambda_{\max}(X_j) \le L$

results.title: Non-commutative Khintchine inequality
results.informal: Moment form of the matrix series bound; sharper for subspace embeddings.

results.title: Distributional JL for a Gaussian sketch
results.informal: For $S = k^{-1/2}G$: $$\mathbb{P}\big[\big|\|Sx\|^2 - \|x\|^2\big| > \varepsilon\|x\|^2\big] \le 2\exp\big(-k(\varepsilon^2/4 - \varepsilon^3/6)\big).$$

results.title: Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma
results.informal: $n$ points embed into $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ dimensions with all pairwise distances preserved to within $1 \pm \varepsilon$; union bound over the distributional lemma.
results.conclusion: there is a linear $S : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^k$ with $(1-\varepsilon)\|p_i - p_j\|^2 \le \|S(p_i - p_j)\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|p_i - p_j\|^2$ for all $i, j$; the Gaussian sketch $k^{-1/2}G$ works with probability at least $1/2$

formalizations.usage: For points `p : Fin N → Fin n → ℝ` and `0 < ε < 1`; bounds the `gaussianMatrix k n`-measure of sketches distorting some pair `i ≠ j` by more than `1 ± ε` by `ENNReal.ofReal (N² · 2 exp(−k(ε²/4 − ε³/6)))` (rests on the `jl_distributional` scaffold).
formalizations.note: union bound over ordered pairs (factor 2 vs N(N−1)/2); explicit constant 48 log N / ε² for failure probability ≤ 1/2; proved modulo the scaffold jl_distributional

Pass `0 < ε < 1`, `hN : 2 ≤ N` and `hk : 48 * log N / ε² ≤ k`; gives that the bad set of Gaussian sketches has measure at most `ENNReal.ofReal (1/2)`.
Pass `0 < ε < 1`, `hN : 2 ≤ N` and `hk : 48 * log N / ε² ≤ k`; gives `∃ S` with `(1 − ε)‖p i − p j‖² ≤ ‖S (p i − p j)‖² ≤ (1 + ε)‖p i − p j‖²` for all `i j` (inherits the `jl_distributional` sorry).

results.notes: Proof complete on top of the distributional lemma; becomes proved automatically once jl_distributional is discharged. All four declarations sorry-free since 2026-10-10.

results.title: Distributional JL for sub-Gaussian sketches
results.informal: Same conclusion for Rademacher and other sub-Gaussian entries, from Hanson–Wright.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{k\times n}$ with independent, centred, unit-variance sub-Gaussian entries and $S = k^{-1/2}A$

results.title: Subspace embedding: definition and equivalent forms
results.informal: $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$ ($U$ orthonormal) iff $\|SUx\|^2 \in (1\pm\varepsilon)\|x\|^2$ for all $x$, iff $\sigma(SU) \subset [\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}, \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}]$, iff $\|U^\top S^\top SU - I\| \le \varepsilon$. Oblivious vs. data-dependent variants.
hypotheses: $S\in\mathbb R^{k\times m}$ and $U\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}$ with $U^\top U=I$
$0\le\varepsilon\le1$ for the singular-value interval; the Gram equivalence only needs $\varepsilon\ge0$
results.conclusion: $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$ iff $(1-\varepsilon)\|x\|^2 \le \|SUx\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|x\|^2$ for all $x$, iff $\sigma(SU) \subset [\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}, \sqrt{1+\varepsilon}]$, iff $\|U^\top S^\top SU - I\| \le \varepsilon$

formalizations.note: Definition, orthonormal-basis form, basis independence and monotonicity; both Gram directions and the singular-value criterion are proved by the additional formalizations below.

formalizations.usage: For S and U over arbitrary finite indices, pass hU : HasOrthonormalCols U and 0≤ε≤1; obtain the interval criterion for every domain singular value of the explicit Fin(card) reindex of S*U.
Pass hU : HasOrthonormalCols U, hε : 0≤ε, and h : IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε; obtain specNorm ((S*U)ᵀ*(S*U)-1)≤ε.
Pass hU : HasOrthonormalCols U and hε : 0≤ε; obtain IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε iff specNorm ((S*U)ᵀ*(S*U)-1)≤ε, over arbitrary finite index types.
Pass `hU : Uᵀ * U = 1`; rewrites `IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε` as `∀ x, (1 − ε) * x ⬝ᵥ x ≤ ‖(S * U) x‖² ∧ ‖(S * U) x‖² ≤ (1 + ε) * x ⬝ᵥ x` (squared norms written with `mulVec` and `⬝ᵥ`).
Pass `hC : IsUnit C.det`; rewrites `IsSubspaceEmbedding S (U * C) ε ↔ IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε` (only the subspace matters).
From `h : IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε` and `hεε' : ε ≤ ε'`; gives `IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε'`.
Pass `hU : Uᵀ * U = 1` and `h : specNorm ((S * U)ᵀ * (S * U) - 1) ≤ ε`; gives `IsSubspaceEmbedding S U ε`.

results.notes: The extension proves both Gram directions and the domain-singular-value equivalence, including empty index types and wide sketches. Domain singular values include kernel zeros.

results.title: Gaussian matrices are oblivious subspace embeddings
results.informal: $k^{-1/2}G$ with $k \ge C(d + \log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon^2$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for any fixed $d$-dimensional subspace with probability $1 - \delta$.
results.conclusion: for $k \ge 18(d + 2\log(2/\delta))/\varepsilon^2$, $k^{-1/2}G$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for a fixed $d$-dimensional subspace with probability at least $1-\delta$

formalizations.usage: Deterministic criterion: `(1-a)‖x‖ ≤ ‖SUx‖ ≤ (1+a)‖x‖` with `3a ≤ ε ≤ 1`.
`k ≥ 18 (d + 2 log(2/δ)) / ε²` gives `1 - δ ≤ P(k^{-1/2} G is an ε-subspace embedding for range U)`; `d = 0` covered.

results.title: Subsampled randomized Hadamard transform is a subspace embedding
results.informal: SRHT with $k = O\big(\varepsilon^{-2}(d + \log n)\log d\big)$ rows is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding. Proof: row flattening by random signs, then matrix Chernoff sampling.
hypotheses: $S = \sqrt{n/k}\,RHD$ with $D$ random signs, $H$ the normalized Walsh–Hadamard matrix, $R$ sampling $k$ rows
results.conclusion: with high probability, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$

results.title: Sparse oblivious subspace embeddings (CountSketch, OSNAP, SparseStack)
results.informal: CountSketch with $k = O(d^2/\varepsilon^2)$ rows is an OSE; OSNAP/SparseStack with $O(d/\varepsilon^2)$ rows and few nonzeros per column.
hypotheses: $S \in \mathbb{R}^{k\times n}$ a CountSketch (one random $\pm 1$ per column) or OSNAP/SparseStack (a few nonzeros per column)
$k = O(d^2/\varepsilon^2)$ for CountSketch, $k = O(d/\varepsilon^2)$ (up to log factors) for OSNAP/SparseStack
results.conclusion: with constant probability, $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(U)$

results.title: Approximate matrix multiplication by row sampling
results.informal: Sampling $c$ column/row pairs with probabilities $p_i \propto \|A_{:,i}\|\,\|B_{i,:}\|$ gives $$\mathbb{E}\|AB - CR\|_F^2 \le \frac{\|A\|_F^2\|B\|_F^2}{c}.$$
hypotheses: $C$, $R$ the sampled columns of $A$ and rows of $B$, rescaled by $1/\sqrt{c\,p_i}$

results.title: Approximate multiplication from a subspace embedding
results.informal: If $S$ satisfies the JL moment property then $$\mathbb{E}\|A^\top S^\top SB - A^\top B\|_F^2 \le \varepsilon^2\|A\|_F^2\|B\|_F^2.$$ The glue between embeddings and least squares.
hypotheses: $S$ satisfies the JL moment property with parameter $\varepsilon$

results.title: Leverage scores: definition and basic properties
aliases: row norms of an orthonormal basis
results.informal: $\ell_i(A) = \|U_{i,:}\|^2 = (AA^\dagger)_{ii}$; $\sum_i \ell_i = \operatorname{rank} A$; $0 \le \ell_i \le 1$; invariant under change of basis of $\operatorname{range}(A)$.
results.conclusion: $\ell_i(A) = \|U_{i,:}\|^2 = (AA^\dagger)_{ii}$, with $\sum_i \ell_i = \operatorname{rank} A$, $0 \le \ell_i \le 1$, independent of the choice of $U$

`∑ i, leverageScore A i = A.rank`.
`ℓᵢ = ∑ j, U i j ^ 2` for any orthonormal basis `U` of `range A`.

results.title: Leverage-score row sampling is a subspace embedding
results.informal: Sampling $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}d\log(d/\delta))$ rows with $p_i \propto \ell_i$ and rescaling gives an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding with probability $1 - \delta$. The same theorem gives spectral sparsification.
hypotheses: $k = O(\varepsilon^{-2}d\log(d/\delta))$ rows sampled i.i.d. with $p_i \propto \ell_i$ and rescaled by $1/\sqrt{kp_i}$
results.conclusion: with probability at least $1 - \delta$, the sampling matrix $S$ is an $\varepsilon$-subspace embedding for $\operatorname{range}(A)$

results.title: Volume sampling and column subset selection
results.informal: Sampling $k$ columns with probability proportional to squared volume gives $$\mathbb{E}\|A - \pi_S(A)\|_F^2 \le (k+1)\,\|A - \lbrack\!\lbrack A \rbrack\!\rbrack_k\|_F^2.$$
hypotheses: a set $S$ of $k$ columns sampled with probability proportional to $\det(A_S^\top A_S)$
$\pi_S$ the orthogonal projection onto the span of the chosen columns

results.informal: For $Y = (AA^\top)^qA\Omega$ and $Q = \operatorname{orth}(Y)$: $$\|(I-QQ^\top)A\| \le \|(I-QQ^\top)(AA^\top)^qA\|^{1/(2q+1)}.$$ Turns the RSVD bound into a bound with $\sigma_{k+1}^{2q+1}$ decay.

HMT Thm 9.2 in power form for any orthonormal `Q`.
`specNorm (residual Q A) ≤ specNorm (residual Q ((A*Aᵀ)^q*A))^(1/(2q+1))`.

results.title: Nyström approximation error for PSD matrices
results.informal: For PSD $A$ and any $\Omega$: $A \succeq A\langle\Omega\rangle := A\Omega(\Omega^\top A\Omega)^\dagger\Omega^\top A \succeq 0$, and $A - A\langle\Omega\rangle$ is the Schur complement. Moreover $\|A - A\langle\Omega\rangle\| \le \|(I-P)A^{1/2}\|^2$ for $P$ the projector onto $\operatorname{range}(A^{1/2}\Omega)$. Foundation for Nyström, RPCholesky and Nyström preconditioning.
results.conclusion: $0 \preceq A\langle\Omega\rangle \preceq A$, $A - A\langle\Omega\rangle$ is a Schur complement, and $\|A - A\langle\Omega\rangle\| \le \|(I-P)A^{1/2}\|^2$

`specNorm (A - nystrom A Ω) = specNorm ((1 - YY⁺) F)^2` (equality).

results.title: Spectral norm of a matrix with sub-Gaussian bilinear marginals
aliases: operator norm via nets and sub-Gaussian marginals
results.informal: If every $u^\top A x$ with unit $u, x$ is $c$-sub-Gaussian then $\mathbb{P}\big[\|A\| > 2(\sqrt{2\log 9\,(m+n)\,c} + \sqrt{c}\,t)\big] \le e^{-t^2/2}$. Net argument with the $(1-2\varepsilon)^{-1}$ bilinear lemma at $\varepsilon = 1/4$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ random with $u^\top A x$ $c$-sub-Gaussian for all unit $u, x$

formalizations.usage: Strict event `2(√(2 log 9 (m+n) c) + √c t) < specNorm A`; `c = 0` handled; any `[Fintype]` indices; no independence assumed.

results.title: Randomized SVD expected spectral error (HMT Thm 10.6)
results.informal: $$\mathbb{E}\|A - QQ^\top A\| \le \Big(1 + \sqrt{\tfrac{k}{p-1}}\Big)\sigma_{k+1} + \frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p}\Big(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\Big)^{1/2}$$ for a Gaussian test matrix with $k+p$ columns, $k, p \ge 2$.
hypotheses: $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times(k+p)}$ standard Gaussian and $Q$ an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{range}(A\Omega)$

formalizations.usage: Block form `(1+√(k/(p-1)))‖Σ₂‖ + (e√(k+p)/p)‖Σ₂‖_F` for any a.s.-orthonormal `Q` whose range a.s. contains `range (AΩ)`; no measurability of `Q` needed.
Singular-value form, `k ≤ n`.
The statement above for `gaussianRangeFrame`.

results.title: Ritz values approximate the largest eigenvalue (gap-free Lanczos bound)
results.informal: The largest Ritz value of $Q^\top AQ$ over $\mathcal K_q(A,b)$ is within $\varepsilon\lambda_1 + \lambda_1\big(\tfrac{2}{(1+\sqrt{2\gamma})^{q-1}}\big)^2\tfrac{\|b\|^2}{\langle u_1,b\rangle^2}$ of $\lambda_1$, $\gamma = \varepsilon/(1-\varepsilon)$: the gap-free form via the Chebyshev amplifier.
hypotheses: $A \succeq 0$ symmetric with top eigenpair $(\lambda_1, u_1)$, $\langle u_1, b\rangle \ne 0$
results.conclusion: some Ritz value $\theta$ of $Q^\top AQ$ satisfies $\lambda_1 - \theta \le \varepsilon\lambda_1 + \lambda_1\Big(\dfrac{2}{(1+\sqrt{2\gamma})^{q-1}}\Big)^2\dfrac{\|b\|^2}{\langle u_1, b\rangle^2}$

formalizations.usage: The underlying Rayleigh-quotient witness in `krylovSpace`.
The bound above for some eigenvalue of `QᵀAQ`.

results.notes: Gap-dependent Kaniel–Paige–Saad form not yet stated. Label check (T1 audit): what is proved is the gap-free bound; the gap-dependent statement Saad Thm 6.4 refers to is `kaniel-paige-saad`.

results.title: Hutch++ is unbiased
results.informal: $\operatorname{tr}(Q^\top AQ) + \hat{\operatorname{tr}}\big((I-QQ^\top)A(I-QQ^\top)\big)$ has expectation $\operatorname{tr}A$ for any orthonormal $Q$, including a random $Q(S)$ independent of the Hutchinson probes.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, $Q$ orthonormal (fixed, or $Q(S)$ with $S$ independent of the probes $G$)

formalizations.usage: Trace split `tr A = tr (QᵀAQ) + tr ((1-QQᵀ)A(1-QQᵀ))`.
Fixed `Q`.
Random `Q(S)` with `S ⊥ G`; product-measure integrability assumed explicitly.

results.title: Randomized Kaczmarz on inconsistent systems
results.informal: For $b = Ax^\star + e$, $\mathbb{E}\|x_k - \hat x\|^2 \le \rho^k\|x_0-\hat x\|^2 + \sum_{j<k}\rho^j\,\|b - A\hat x\|^2/\|A\|_F^2$ for any $\hat x$, hence a convergence horizon $\|e\|^2/\sigma^2$.

formalizations.usage: `ρ^k ‖x - x̂‖² + (∑_{j<k} ρ^j) ‖b - A x̂‖²/‖A‖_F²` for any `x̂`.
The `+ ‖e‖²/σ²` horizon form.

results.title: Randomized Kaczmarz on rank-deficient systems converges to the least-norm solution
results.informal: Started at $x_0 = 0$, the iterates stay in $\operatorname{range}A^\top$ and $\mathbb{E}\|x_k - A^+b\|^2 \le (1 - 1/(\|A^+\|^2\|A\|_F^2))^k\|A^+b\|^2$, with no rank assumption.

formalizations.usage: The rate needs `hσ` only on `range Aᵀ`.
Convergence to `A⁺ b` from `x₀ = 0`.

results.title: Frobenius and spectral norms
results.informal: $\|A\|_F^2 = \sum_{ij} A_{ij}^2$, $\langle A, B\rangle_F = \operatorname{tr}(A^\top B)$, and the spectral norm $\|A\|_2 = \max_{\|x\|_2 = 1} \|Ax\|_2$ of a real matrix.

results.title: Orthonormal columns
results.informal: $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times k}$ has orthonormal columns when $Q^\top Q = I_k$; then $QQ^\top$ is the orthogonal projector onto $\operatorname{range} Q$.

results.title: Residual of a projection
results.informal: $\operatorname{residual}(Q, A) = (I - QQ^\top) A$: the part of $A$ outside $\operatorname{range} Q$, the quantity every range-finder bound controls.

results.title: SVD predicate and singular values
results.informal: $A = U \Sigma V^\top$ with $U, V$ orthogonal and $\Sigma$ rectangular diagonal with $\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \dots \ge 0$; $\sigma_i(A)$ is the $i$-th singular value and $\sigma_{\min}(A)^2 = \lambda_{\min}(A^\top A)$.

results.title: Best rank-k approximation and the singular-value tail
results.informal: $[\![A]\!]_k = U_k \Sigma_k V_k^\top$ is a best rank-$k$ approximation; $\|A - [\![A]\!]_k\|_F^2 = \sum_{j > k} \sigma_j(A)^2$ is the squared singular-value tail that randomized low-rank bounds are measured against.

results.title: Quadratic form xᵀAx
results.informal: $\operatorname{quadForm}(A, x) = x^\top A x$, the random variable whose mean is $\operatorname{tr} A$ for isotropic $x$ (trace estimation) and whose tails Hanson–Wright controls.

results.title: Spectral quantities and matrix functions (complex Hermitian)
results.informal: $\lambda_{\max}$, $\lambda_{\min}$, $\|\cdot\|$, the Loewner order $A \preceq B$, and the standard matrix functions $e^A$, $\log A$, $\operatorname{tr} e^A$, $f(A)$ via the continuous functional calculus, as used by the matrix Laplace-transform method.

results.title: Standard Gaussian and Rademacher laws
results.informal: Predicates on real random variables: $g \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ and $\varepsilon$ uniform on $\{\pm 1\}$ (the Rademacher measure), the two isotropic laws used for matrix series and trace estimators.

results.title: Trace estimators: Hutchinson, Hutch++, SLQ
results.informal: $\operatorname{tr} A \approx \frac1m \sum_{i=1}^m x_i^\top A x_i$ for isotropic probes $x_i$ (Hutchinson), its variance-reduced form Hutch++, the row-selector form for diagonal estimation, and the SLQ estimate of $\operatorname{tr} f(A)$ from Gauss quadrature.

results.title: Randomized Kaczmarz iteration
results.informal: $x_{t+1} = x_t - \frac{(a_i^\top x_t - b_i)}{\|a_i\|^2} a_i$ with row $i$ drawn with probability $\|a_i\|^2 / \|A\|_F^2$; the expected squared error $\mathbb{E}\|x_t - x^\star\|^2$ and the Frobenius condition number $\|A\|_F \|A^+\|$ that govern its rate.

results.title: Regularized Gram soft-min and inverse-power potentials
results.informal: Definitions behind the inverse-power Gram results: `regularizedGram`: A Gram matrix regularized by a scalar multiple of the identity.; `inversePowerSoftMin`: Resolvent approximation to the smallest eigenvalue: the negative `n`th root of the inverse-power trace.; `gramSoftMinGradient`: The coordinate gradient of the resolvent regularized Gram functional.

results.notes: Consumers: gmres-def (finite termination), arnoldi-relation (breakdown iff h_{q+1,q} = 0 iff q = ν), lanczos-recurrence (the non-breakdown hypothesis `LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i => A^i b)` of `hasOrthonormalCols_lanczosMatrix` is exactly q ≤ ν), krylov-polynomial-exactness, gmres-any-convergence-curve, cg-convergence (finite termination). Prove.

results.title: Arnoldi basis and Hessenberg matrices
results.informal: The Arnoldi basis $Q_q = [q_1,\dots,q_q]$ is the Gram–Schmidt orthonormalisation of $b, Ab, \dots, A^{q-1}b$; $H_q = Q_q^\top A Q_q \in \mathbb R^{q\times q}$ and $\underline H_q = Q_{q+1}^\top A Q_q \in \mathbb R^{(q+1)\times q}$. A matrix is upper Hessenberg if $h_{ij} = 0$ for $i > j+1$. Characterisations: $Q_q$ has orthonormal columns spanning $\mathcal K_q(A,b)$ when $q \le \nu$, $H_q$ and $\underline H_q$ are upper Hessenberg, $h_{j+1,j} = \|(I - Q_jQ_j^\top)Aq_j\| \ge 0$ with equality iff $j \ge \nu$, and the basis is unique up to signs (implicit-Q uniqueness: positive subdiagonal fixes it).
hypotheses: for orthonormality and the Hessenberg sign/uniqueness statements: $q+1 \le \nu(A,b)$ (no breakdown)
results.conclusion: $Q_q^\top Q_q = I$, $\operatorname{range}Q_q = \mathcal K_q(A,b)$, $H_q$ and $\underline H_q$ upper Hessenberg with $h_{j+1,j} > 0$ for $j < \nu$; any $\tilde Q$ with orthonormal columns, $\tilde Q e_1 = b/\|b\|$ and $\tilde Q^\top A\tilde Q$ upper Hessenberg with positive subdiagonal equals $Q_q$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Already used by `NLAlib.lanczosBasis`.
No Hessenberg predicate in Mathlib (grep for Hessenberg finds nothing).

results.notes: NLAlib's `lanczosMatrix A b q` is already the Arnoldi basis for every real A: `lanczos_apply_eq_zero_of_add_one_lt` proves QᵀAQ is upper Hessenberg without symmetry. So this entry is mostly naming (`arnoldiMatrix := lanczosMatrix`, `hessenberg A b q := Qᵀ A Q`, the extended (q+1)×q matrix) plus the positive-subdiagonal and uniqueness characterisations. Consumers: arnoldi-relation, fom-def, arnoldi-fa-error, lanczos-recurrence, gmres-def (the least-squares form ‖βe₁ − H̲_q y‖). Prove.

results.title: Arnoldi relation AQ_q = Q_qH_q + h_{q+1,q} q_{q+1} e_qᵀ
results.informal: With the Arnoldi basis, $$AQ_q = Q_{q+1}\underline H_q = Q_qH_q + h_{q+1,q}\,q_{q+1}e_q^\top,$$ and $Q_q^\top AQ_q = H_q$. Arnoldi breaks down at step $q$ ($h_{q+1,q} = 0$) iff $q = \nu(A,b)$, in which case $AQ_q = Q_qH_q$ and $\mathcal K_q$ is $A$-invariant. For symmetric $A$, $H_q = T_q$ is the symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix and the relation is the Lanczos three-term recurrence $Aq_j = \beta_{j-1}q_{j-1} + \alpha_jq_j + \beta_jq_{j+1}$.
hypotheses: $q + 1 \le \nu(A,b)$ for the extended form (so $q_{q+1}$ exists); $q \le \nu$ and $h_{q+1,q} := 0$ otherwise
results.conclusion: $AQ_q = Q_qH_q + h_{q+1,q}q_{q+1}e_q^\top = Q_{q+1}\underline H_q$; $h_{q+1,q} = 0 \iff q = \nu(A,b)$; for $A = A^\top$: $H_q$ is symmetric tridiagonal and $Aq_j = \beta_{j-1}q_{j-1} + \alpha_jq_j + \beta_jq_{j+1}$ with $\beta_j = h_{j+1,j}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Q Qᵀ x = x for x in the span; NLAlib already has the matrix form `mulVec_transpose_mulVec_of_mem_range`.

results.notes: Closes the open half of the existing candidate `lanczos-recurrence` (whose notes say the identity AQ_q = Q_qT_q + β_q q_{q+1}e_qᵀ is not yet stated); that entry should gain `depends_on: arnoldi-relation`. Column j of the identity is A q_j ∈ K_{j+1} = span(q_1..q_{j+1}) expanded in the orthonormal basis, so the proof is short given `range_lanczosMatrix` and the Hessenberg lemma. Consumers: lanczos-recurrence, fom-def, gmres-def (least-squares form), krylov-polynomial-exactness, arnoldi-fa-error, Lanczos-based SLQ (`slq-error`) when written with the recurrence. Prove.

results.title: Krylov projection is exact on low-degree polynomials; the Ritz polynomial minimises ‖p(A)b‖
results.informal: If $Q$ has orthonormal columns with $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$ and $H = Q^\top AQ$, then $p(A)b = Q\,p(H)\,Q^\top b$ for every $p$ with $\deg p < q$, and $Q^\top p(A)b = p(H)Q^\top b$ for $\deg p \le q$. If moreover $\operatorname{range}Q = \mathcal K_q(A,b)$ with $q \le \nu$, the characteristic polynomial $\chi_H$ is the unique monic $p$ of degree $q$ minimising $\|p(A)b\|$.
hypotheses: $Q \in \mathbb R^{n\times k}$ with $Q^\top Q = I$ and $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$; $H = Q^\top AQ$
for the minimality clause: $\operatorname{range}Q = \mathcal K_q(A,b)$ and $q \le \nu(A,b)$
results.conclusion: $p(A)b = Q\,p(H)\,Q^\top b$ for $\deg p < q$; $Q^\top p(A)b = p(H)\,Q^\top b$ for $\deg p \le q$; $\|\chi_H(A)b\| = \min\{\|p(A)b\| : p \text{ monic}, \deg p = q\}$ with $\chi_H(A)b \perp \mathcal K_q$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Cayley–Hamilton for H gives χ_H(H) = 0, hence Qᵀχ_H(A)b = 0.
Minimiser over the affine set {A^q b + K_q} iff orthogonal to K_q.

results.notes: The power form `Q (QᵀAQ)^j Qᵀ b = A^j b` (j < q, any real A) is already proved as `NLAlib.mulVec_pow_transpose_mul_mul_mulVec_eq` (helper of lanczos-gauss-quadrature); this entry packages the polynomial form, the degree-q projected identity and the monic-minimality (Arnoldi/Lanczos eigenvalue) characterisation as public statements. Consumers: lanczos-fa-error, arnoldi-fa-error, fom-def (the FOM iterate is x₀ + Q H⁻¹ Qᵀ r₀), lanczos-gauss-quadrature (could be refactored onto it). Prove.

results.title: Block Krylov subspaces and their matrix-polynomial characterisation
results.informal: For $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $\Omega \in \mathbb R^{n\times s}$, $\mathcal K_q(A,\Omega) = \operatorname{range}[\Omega, A\Omega, \dots, A^{q-1}\Omega] = \sum_{j=1}^s \mathcal K_q(A,\omega_j) = \{\sum_{i<q}A^i\Omega C_i : C_i \in \mathbb R^{s\times s'}\}$. It contains $\operatorname{range}(p(A)\Omega)$ for every scalar polynomial $p$ with $\deg p < q$, is nested in $q$, satisfies $A\mathcal K_q \subseteq \mathcal K_{q+1}$, and has dimension at most $qs$. The rectangular form used for low-rank approximation is $\mathcal K_q(AA^\top, A\Omega) \ni \varphi(AA^\top)A\Omega$ for $\deg\varphi < q$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $\Omega \in \mathbb R^{n\times s}$, $q \in \mathbb N$ (rectangular case: $A \in \mathbb R^{m\times n}$ and the space $\mathcal K_q(AA^\top, A\Omega)$)
results.conclusion: $\mathcal K_q(A,\Omega) = \sum_j \mathcal K_q(A,\Omega e_j)$; $\operatorname{range}(p(A)\Omega) \subseteq \mathcal K_q(A,\Omega)$ for $\deg p < q$; $\mathcal K_q \subseteq \mathcal K_{q+1}$, $A\mathcal K_q \subseteq \mathcal K_{q+1}$, $\dim\mathcal K_q \le qs$
results.notes: Define as `⨆ j, krylovSpace A (fun r => Ω r j) q` so every single-vector lemma transfers. Consumers: polynomial-filter-range-finder, block-krylov-lra (Musco–Musco Thm 1), subspace-iteration-expected (q = 1 slice), randomized block Krylov trace estimation (Krylov-aware Hutch++). Prove.

results.title: Residual polynomials and the min–max quantity ε_k(S)
results.informal: $\mathcal P_k^0 = \{p \in \mathbb R[x] : \deg p \le k,\ p(0) = 1\}$ and, for $S \subseteq \mathbb C$, $\varepsilon_k(S) = \inf_{p\in\mathcal P_k^0}\sup_{z\in S}|p(z)|$. Characterisation: $x \in x_0 + \mathcal K_k(A, r_0)$ iff $b - Ax = p(A)r_0$ for some $p \in \mathcal P_k^0$ (and then $x - x_\star = p(A)(x_0 - x_\star)$ when $Ax_\star = b$). $\varepsilon_k$ is antitone in $k$, monotone in $S$, attained for finite or compact $S$, and $\varepsilon_k([a,b]) = 1/T_k\big(\tfrac{b+a}{b-a}\big)$ for $0<a<b$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $b, x_0 \in \mathbb R^n$, $r_0 = b - Ax_0$, $k \in \mathbb N$
results.conclusion: $x - x_0 \in \mathcal K_k(A,r_0) \iff \exists p \in \mathcal P_k^0,\ b - Ax = p(A)r_0$; $\varepsilon_{k+1}(S) \le \varepsilon_k(S)$; $S \subseteq S' \Rightarrow \varepsilon_k(S) \le \varepsilon_k(S')$; the infimum is a minimum for finite $S$; $\varepsilon_k([a,b]) = 1/T_k(\frac{b+a}{b-a})$
results.notes: The affine-Krylov ↔ residual-polynomial step is currently a private lemma inside `NLAlib/Krylov/CG.lean` (`exists_degree_lt_one_sub_eq_X_mul`); making it public removes duplication. The value ε_k([a,b]) is the existing `isLeast_chebyshev_minimax`. Consumers (highest in-degree of this group): gmres-def, gmres-diagonalizable, gmres-elman, gmres-bgt, crouzeix-palencia (GMRES corollary), minres-bound, chebyshev-iteration, richardson-iteration, fom-def, cg-convergence (refactor). Prove.

results.title: GMRES iterate: residual minimisation over the Krylov space
results.informal:
$x_k$ is a GMRES iterate if $x_k \in x_0 + \mathcal K_k(A,r_0)$ and $\|b - Ax_k\|_2 \le \|b - Ax\|_2$ for all $x \in x_0 + \mathcal K_k(A,r_0)$. Characterisations: an iterate exists for every $A$; the residual $r_k$ is unique and $x_k$ is unique if $A$ is invertible; $r_k \perp A\mathcal K_k(A,r_0)$ (Petrov–Galerkin); $\|r_k\| = \min_{p\in\mathcal P_k^0}\|p(A)r_0\|$; $\|r_{k+1}\| \le \|r_k\|$; with Arnoldi, $\|r_k\| = \min_y\|\,\|r_0\|e_1 - \underline H_k y\|$; if $A$ is invertible, $r_
u = 0$ at the grade $
u = 
u(A,r_0)$. For symmetric $A$ this is MINRES.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $b, x_0 \in \mathbb R^n$, $r_0 = b - Ax_0$, $k \in \mathbb N$ (complex form: $\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with the Hermitian inner product)
results.conclusion: existence; uniqueness of $r_k$ (and of $x_k$ if $A$ invertible); $r_k \perp A\mathcal K_k$; $\|r_k\| = \min_{p\in\mathcal P_k^0}\|p(A)r_0\|$; $\|r_{k+1}\| \le \|r_k\|$; $\|r_k\| = \min_y\|\,\|r_0\|e_1 - \underline H_ky\|$; $A$ invertible $\Rightarrow r_{\nu(A,r_0)} = 0$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Existence of the minimiser (Hilbert projection) applied to the finite-dimensional subspace A·K_k.
Petrov–Galerkin characterisation r_k ⟂ A K_k.

results.notes: Mirror `NLAlib.IsCGIterate` (variational definition, existence by projection, no algorithm). Real primary statement: for real A, b, x₀ the real GMRES residual equals the complex one (for real r₀, replacing a complex p by its real-coefficient part never increases ‖p(A)r₀‖), so complex-spectrum bounds (gmres-diagonalizable, gmres-bgt, crouzeix-palencia) apply to the real definition. Consumers: gmres-diagonalizable, gmres-elman, gmres-bgt, minres-bound, gmres-any-convergence-curve, restarted GMRES(m) (Elman per cycle), sketched GMRES (Nakatsukasa–Tropp 2024: minimise ‖S(b − AQy)‖ over a Krylov basis; a sketch-and-solve consumer with `sketch-and-solve-ls`). The Arnoldi least-squares clause can be split off if arnoldi-relation lags. Prove.

results.title: GMRES bound for diagonalisable A: ‖r_k‖ ≤ κ(V) ε_k(Λ) ‖r_0‖
results.informal: If $A = V\Lambda V^{-1}$ with $\Lambda = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)$, then the GMRES residual satisfies $$\frac{\|r_k\|}{\|r_0\|} \le \min_{p\in\mathcal P_k^0}\|p(A)\| \le \kappa_2(V)\min_{p\in\mathcal P_k^0}\max_i|p(\lambda_i)|.$$ For normal $A$ ($V$ unitary) the factor is $1$, and the bound is then sharp in the worst case over $r_0$ (Greenbaum–Gurvits, Joubert).
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $V \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$ invertible, $\lambda \in \mathbb C^n$ with $A = V\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)V^{-1}$ over $\mathbb C$
results.conclusion: $\|r_k\| \le \|V\|_2\|V^{-1}\|_2\,\max_i|p(\lambda_i)|\,\|r_0\|$ for every real $p \in \mathcal P_k^0$; for $A$ normal, $\|r_k\| \le \max_i|p(\lambda_i)|\,\|r_0\|$

mathlib_prereqs.note: No matrix diagonalisability predicate; state with an explicit V and diagonal Λ.

results.notes: Over real p the min–max over a conjugation-closed spectrum equals the complex one, so the real statement loses nothing. For symmetric A this is the general clause of minres-bound and can reuse `specNorm_aeval_le`. The worst-case sharpness for normal A (max over ‖r₀‖=1 of ‖r_k‖ equals ε_k(σ(A)); Greenbaum–Gurvits 1994) is a later, harder (4) variant: assume if needed. Consumers: minres-bound, gmres-bgt (comparison), sketched GMRES analyses, Krylov solvers inside randomized preconditioning of nonsymmetric systems. Prove.

results.title: Elman bound: GMRES for positive-real A
results.informal: If the symmetric part $M = (A + A^\top)/2$ is positive definite, then $$\|r_k\| \le \Big(1 - \frac{\lambda_{\min}(M)^2}{\|A\|_2^2}\Big)^{k/2}\|r_0\|.$$ The same bound holds for restarted GMRES($m$) after $k$ total steps, since each cycle contracts by the per-step factor.
results.conclusion: $\|r_k\| \le (1 - \alpha^2/\beta^2)^{k/2}\|r_0\|$; for GMRES($m$) restarted every $m$ steps, $\|r^{(j)}\| \le (1 - \alpha^2/\beta^2)^{jm/2}\|r_0\|$ after $j$ cycles
results.notes: Proof: ‖(I − ωA)r‖² ≤ (1 − 2ωα + ω²β²)‖r‖², take ω = α/β², and p(z) = (1 − ωz)^k ∈ P_k^0. Entirely real; no field of values needed (the complex form with dist(0, W(A)) in place of α is a variant under field-of-values-def). Consumers: restarted GMRES, gmres-bgt (it is the bound BGT sharpen), preconditioned nonsymmetric solves where the preconditioned operator is positive real. Prove.

results.title: MINRES bounds: spectral min–max and two indefinite intervals
results.informal: For symmetric invertible $A$, the minimal-residual (MINRES = GMRES) iterate satisfies $\|r_k\| \le \min_{p\in\mathcal P_k^0}\max_i|p(\lambda_i)|\,\|r_0\|$. If the spectrum lies in $[a,b]\cup[c,d]$ with $a<b<0<c<d$ and $b-a = d-c$, then $$\|r_{2k}\| \le 2\Big(\frac{\sqrt{|ad|}-\sqrt{|bc|}}{\sqrt{|ad|}+\sqrt{|bc|}}\Big)^k\|r_0\|,$$ in particular $2\big(\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1}\big)^k$ for $[-d,-c]\cup[c,d]$, $\kappa = d/c$; for $A \succ 0$ with spectrum in $[a,b]$, $\|r_k\| \le 2\big(\frac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\big)^k\|r_0\|$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric and invertible, $x_k$ a GMRES iterate (gmres-def)
for the interval clauses: every eigenvalue in $[a,b]\cup[c,d]$, $a<b<0<c<d$, $d - c = b - a$ (resp. in $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$)
results.conclusion: $\|r_k\| \le \max_i|p(\lambda_i)|\,\|r_0\|$ for every $p \in \mathcal P_k^0$; $\|r_{2k}\| \le 2\big(\frac{\sqrt{|ad|}-\sqrt{|bc|}}{\sqrt{|ad|}+\sqrt{|bc|}}\big)^k\|r_0\|$; definite case $\|r_k\| \le 2\big(\frac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\big)^k\|r_0\|$
results.notes: Each clause is polynomial-spectral-bound applied to the GMRES polynomial characterisation plus a polynomial from two-interval-minimax or chebyshev-minimax. Consumers: preconditioned MINRES for saddle-point / KKT systems, LSMR (MINRES on the normal equations) inside sketch-and-precondition least squares, regularised indefinite solves in randomized Newton methods. Prove.

results.title: FOM (Arnoldi Galerkin) iterate and its residual formula
results.informal: $x_k^F$ is a FOM iterate if $x_k^F \in x_0 + \mathcal K_k(A,r_0)$ and $b - Ax_k^F \perp \mathcal K_k(A,r_0)$. It exists and is unique iff $H_k$ is invertible, and then $x_k^F = x_0 + \|r_0\|Q_kH_k^{-1}e_1$ and $r_k^F = -h_{k+1,k}\,(e_k^\top H_k^{-1}e_1)\|r_0\|\,q_{k+1}$. For symmetric positive definite $A$ the FOM iterate is the CG iterate.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $b, x_0$, $r_0 = b - Ax_0 \ne 0$, $1 \le k \le \nu(A,r_0)$, Arnoldi data $Q_k, H_k, h_{k+1,k}, q_{k+1}$
results.conclusion: a FOM iterate exists uniquely iff $\det H_k \ne 0$; then $x_k^F = x_0 + \|r_0\|Q_kH_k^{-1}e_1$, $\|r_k^F\| = h_{k+1,k}\,|e_k^\top H_k^{-1}e_1|\,\|r_0\|$; if $A$ is symmetric positive definite, $x_k^F$ satisfies `IsCGIterate A b x₀ k`
results.notes: FOM is the Arnoldi approximation of f(A)b for f(z) = 1/z, so it ties the f(A)b entries to linear solves. Later variant (identity, difficulty 3): the Brown / Cullum–Greenbaum peak–plateau relation ‖r_k^F‖ = ‖r_k^G‖ / √(1 − (‖r_k^G‖/‖r_{k−1}^G‖)²), with FOM undefined exactly when GMRES stagnates (Saad 2003 §6.5.7). Consumers: lanczos-fa-error for 1/x, sketched FOM, the identification of CG as Galerkin (cg-convergence). Prove.

results.title: Chebyshev semi-iterative method: residual polynomial and rate
results.informal: For $A$ symmetric with spectrum in $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$, let $\theta = \tfrac{b+a}2$, $\delta = \tfrac{b-a}2$, $\sigma = \theta/\delta$, $\rho_0 = 1/\sigma$, $\rho_k = 1/(2\sigma - \rho_{k-1})$, $d_0 = r_0/\theta$, $d_k = \rho_k\rho_{k-1}d_{k-1} + \tfrac{2\rho_k}{\delta}r_k$, $x_{k+1} = x_k + d_k$. Then $r_k = R_k(A)r_0$ with $R_k(t) = T_k\big(\tfrac{\theta - t}{\delta}\big)/T_k(\sigma)$ (NLAlib `chebyshevResidual a b k`), so $$\|r_k\| \le \frac{\|r_0\|}{T_k(\sigma)} \le 2\Big(\frac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\Big)^k\|r_0\|,$$ and the same for the error in the $A$-norm. No inner products are needed.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric with all eigenvalues in $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$
$x_0$ arbitrary and $x_k$ produced by the recurrence above (Saad Alg. 12.1)
results.conclusion: $b - Ax_k = R_k(A)(b - Ax_0)$ with $R_k = $ `chebyshevResidual a b k`; $\|r_k\| \le 2\big(\frac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\big)^k\|r_0\|$ and $\|x_k - x_\star\|_A \le 2\big(\frac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\big)^k\|x_0 - x_\star\|_A$

mathlib_prereqs.note: The three-term recurrence of T_k drives the identity r_k = R_k(A) r_0.

results.notes: The identity is an induction on the coupled recurrences (the ρ_k bookkeeping is the work). Preconditioned form: replace A by P⁻¹A with aP ≼ A ≼ bP. Consumers: LSRN (Meng–Saunders–Mahoney 2014) runs Chebyshev semi-iteration on the sketch-preconditioned normal equations; polynomial preconditioning and Chebyshev filtering in subspace iteration; the kernel polynomial method for spectral densities (same recurrence). Prove.

results.title: Preconditioned Richardson iteration: error contraction
results.informal: For $A, P$ symmetric positive definite with $aP \preceq A \preceq bP$ and step $\omega > 0$, the iteration $x_{k+1} = x_k + \omega P^{-1}(c - Ax_k)$ has $x_k - x_\star = (I - \omega P^{-1}A)^k(x_0 - x_\star)$ and $$\|x_k - x_\star\|_A \le \rho(\omega)^k\|x_0 - x_\star\|_A,\qquad \rho(\omega) = \max(|1-\omega a|, |1-\omega b|),$$ also in the $P$-norm; $\omega = 2/(a+b)$ gives $\rho = \frac{b-a}{b+a}$. $P = I$ is plain Richardson.
hypotheses: $A, P \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric positive definite, $0 < a \le b$, $aP \preceq A \preceq bP$ (Loewner)
results.conclusion: $x_k - x_\star = (I - \omega P^{-1}A)^k(x_0 - x_\star)$; $\|x_k - x_\star\|_A \le \max(|1-\omega a|,|1-\omega b|)^k\|x_0 - x_\star\|_A$ (same in $\|\cdot\|_P$); with $\omega = \frac2{a+b}$ the factor is $\frac{b-a}{b+a}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: P^{1/2} to symmetrise P^{-1}A; or use LDL.lower_conj_diag for P = LLᵀ.

results.notes: The symmetrisation P^{-1/2}AP^{-1/2} with spectrum in [a,b] reduces it to polynomial-spectral-bound with p(t) = (1 − ωt)^k. Consumers: iterative sketching for least squares (Pilanci–Wainwright iterative Hessian sketch; Epperly 2024 'fast and forward stable' iterative sketching with P = (SA)ᵀ(SA), A ↦ AᵀA, a = (1+ε)^{-2}, b = (1−ε)^{-2} from `ose-def`), sketch-and-project viewed as preconditioned Richardson, damped Newton–sketch. Momentum (heavy-ball) acceleration is a later variant. Prove.

results.title: CGLS / LSQR convergence: κ(A)-rate for least squares
results.informal: For $A \in \mathbb R^{m\times n}$ of full column rank with singular values in $[\sigma_{lo},\sigma_{hi}]$, the iterate $x_k$ minimising $\|b - Ax\|$ over $x_0 + \mathcal K_k(A^\top A, A^\top(b - Ax_0))$ (CGLS/LSQR in exact arithmetic) satisfies $$\|A(x_k - x_\star)\| \le 2\Big(\frac{\sigma_{hi}-\sigma_{lo}}{\sigma_{hi}+\sigma_{lo}}\Big)^k\|A(x_0 - x_\star)\|,$$ $x_\star = \arg\min\|b - Ax\|$, and $\|b - Ax_k\|^2 = \|b - Ax_\star\|^2 + \|A(x_k - x_\star)\|^2$. With a right preconditioner $R$ the same holds with the singular values of $AR^{-1}$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $\operatorname{rank}A = n$, all singular values in $[\sigma_{lo},\sigma_{hi}]$, $0 < \sigma_{lo} \le \sigma_{hi}$
$x_k$ = `IsCGIterate (AᵀA) (Aᵀb) x₀ k`, equivalently the minimiser of $\|b - Ax\|$ over $x_0 + \mathcal K_k(A^\top A, A^\top(b - Ax_0))$
results.conclusion: $\|A(x_k - x_\star)\| \le 2\big(\frac{\sigma_{hi}-\sigma_{lo}}{\sigma_{hi}+\sigma_{lo}}\big)^k\|A(x_0 - x_\star)\|$ and $\|b - Ax_k\|^2 = \|b - Ax_\star\|^2 + \|A(x_k - x_\star)\|^2$

mathlib_prereqs.note: AᵀA ≻ 0 from full column rank.

results.notes: A direct instance of `quadForm_sub_le_of_isCGIterate(_of_le)` with A ↦ AᵀA, c = Aᵀb, a = σ_lo², b = σ_hi² (√ of the eigenvalue ratio is the singular value ratio). This is the Krylov solver of Blendenpik / LSRN / sketch-and-precondition: with R from a QR of SA and S an ε-embedding, κ(AR⁻¹) ≤ (1+ε)/(1−ε), so O(log(1/δ)) iterations suffice; the existing candidate `sketch-and-precondition` becomes an end-to-end result once this is in. Prove.

results.title: Preconditioned CG bound under a Loewner sandwich aP ≼ A ≼ bP
results.informal: For $A, P \succ 0$ with $aP \preceq A \preceq bP$, the PCG iterate (minimiser of $\|x - x_\star\|_A$ over $x_0 + \mathcal K_k(P^{-1}A, P^{-1}r_0)$) satisfies $$\|x_k - x_\star\|_A \le 2\Big(\frac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\Big)^k\|x_0 - x_\star\|_A.$$ Equivalently CG applied to $L^{-1}AL^{-\top}$ for any factorisation $P = LL^\top$, with $\mathcal K_k(P^{-1}A, P^{-1}r_0) = L^{-\top}\mathcal K_k(L^{-1}AL^{-\top}, L^{-1}r_0)$.
hypotheses: $A, P \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric positive definite, $0 < a < b$ (or $\le$), $aP \preceq A \preceq bP$
$Ax_\star = c$; $x_k$ minimises `cgObjective A c` over $x_0 + \mathcal K_k(P^{-1}A, P^{-1}(c - Ax_0))$
results.conclusion: $\|x_k - x_\star\|_A \le 2\big(\frac{\sqrt b-\sqrt a}{\sqrt b+\sqrt a}\big)^k\|x_0 - x_\star\|_A$; the PCG Krylov space is the image under $L^{-\top}$ of the CG Krylov space of $L^{-1}AL^{-\top}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: LDLᵀ factorisation of a positive definite matrix gives P = LLᵀ after absorbing √D.
Alternative symmetric factor P^{1/2}.

results.notes: The Loewner-sandwich hypothesis is how randomized preconditioners are certified, so stating it that way avoids a generalised-eigenvalue API. Consumers: `nystrom-pcg` (Frangella–Tropp–Udell: (A + μI) vs Nyström preconditioner, a and b from the Nyström error), randomly pivoted Cholesky preconditioning, sketch-and-precondition when solved by CG on normal equations (with cgls-lsqr-bound). Prove.

results.title: Residual polynomial small on two intervals of equal length
results.informal: For $a<b<0<c<d$ with $d - c = b - a$ and $k \in \mathbb N$, $p(x) = R_k\big(x^2 - (b+c)x\big)$, with $R_k$ the shifted Chebyshev residual on $[\,|bc|, |ad|\,]$, has $\deg p \le 2k$, $p(0) = 1$ and $$\max_{x\in[a,b]\cup[c,d]}|p(x)| \le 2\Big(\frac{\sqrt{|ad|}-\sqrt{|bc|}}{\sqrt{|ad|}+\sqrt{|bc|}}\Big)^k.$$ The map $x \mapsto x^2 - (b+c)x$ sends both intervals onto $[\,|bc|, |ad|\,]$ and $0 \mapsto 0$. For $[-d,-c]\cup[c,d]$ the bound is $2\big(\frac{d-c}{d+c}\big)^k$.
hypotheses: $a < b < 0 < c < d$ with $d - c = b - a$, $k \in \mathbb N$
results.notes: Direct from `abs_eval_chebyshevResidual_le_two_mul_pow` with interval [|bc|, |ad|] composed with the quadratic (check: (d−b)(d−c) − bc = |ad| uses d − c = b − a). Optimality (it is the min–max value for equal-length intervals) is a later, harder variant. Belongs to the polynomial layer; group T2 may also list indefinite approximation, deduplicate on merge. Consumers: minres-bound, indefinite Lanczos-FA bounds, spectrum-slicing filters. Prove.

results.title: Field of values (numerical range) and its basic properties
results.informal: $W(A) = \{x^*Ax : x \in \mathbb C^n, \|x\| = 1\}$ for $A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$ (for real $A$, of its complexification). Properties: compact; contains every eigenvalue; $W(A) \subseteq \{|z| \le \|A\|_2\}$; $W(\alpha A + \beta I) = \alpha W(A) + \beta$; $W(U^*AU) = W(A)$ for unitary $U$; $W(Q^*AQ) \subseteq W(A)$ for $Q$ with orthonormal columns (compressions, Arnoldi $H_q$); $\operatorname{Re}W(A) = [\lambda_{\min}(M), \lambda_{\max}(M)]$, $M = \tfrac12(A + A^*)$; convex (Toeplitz–Hausdorff); $W(A) = \operatorname{conv}\sigma(A)$ for normal $A$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$ over a `Fintype` index (real $A$ via `A.map Complex.ofReal`)
results.conclusion: $W(A)$ is compact and convex, $\sigma(A) \subseteq W(A) \subseteq \bar B(0,\|A\|_2)$, $W(Q^*AQ) \subseteq W(A)$ for $Q^*Q = I$, $\operatorname{Re}W(A) = [\lambda_{\min}(M),\lambda_{\max}(M)]$, and $W(A) = \operatorname{conv}\sigma(A)$ if $A$ is normal

mathlib_prereqs.note: Mathlib has no numerical range / field of values (grep for numericalRange, fieldOfValues, numericalRadius finds nothing).

results.notes: Intrinsically complex. Everything except convexity is difficulty 1–2; Toeplitz–Hausdorff convexity (reduce to 2×2) is the difficulty-3 piece and is not needed by the assumed consumers, so it can land last. Consumers: crouzeix-palencia, gmres-bgt, arnoldi-fa-error, the complex form of gmres-elman (dist(0, W(A)) in place of λ_min(M)), pseudospectral/numerical-range arguments in non-normal randomized NLA (e.g. sketched Arnoldi eigen-solvers). Prove.

results.title: Crouzeix–Palencia: W(A) is a (1+√2)-spectral set
aliases: numerical range is a K-spectral set
results.informal: For every $A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$ and every polynomial $p$, $$\|p(A)\|_2 \le (1+\sqrt2)\max_{z\in W(A)}|p(z)|.$$ Consequently the GMRES residual satisfies $\|r_k\| \le (1+\sqrt2)\,\varepsilon_k(W(A))\,\|r_0\|$. (Crouzeix conjectures the constant 2.)

mathlib_prereqs.note: Maximum modulus; part of any proof via the Cauchy transform on ∂W(A).

results.notes: Assume (status `assumed` once a consumer is formalised): the statement is short, polynomial-only (no holomorphic functional calculus needed) and certain; the proof (Cauchy-transform / double-layer potential on the boundary of a convex set) is research-level to formalise. Stating it for polynomials sidesteps Mathlib's lack of a functional calculus for non-normal matrices. Consumers: arnoldi-fa-error, the GMRES field-of-values bound above, non-normal Krylov f(A)b and trace-of-f(A) estimators for nonsymmetric A.

results.title: Beckermann–Goreinov–Tyrtyshnikov sharpening of the Elman bound
results.informal: If $0 \notin W(A)$ and $\beta \in [0,\pi/2)$ is defined by $\cos\beta = \operatorname{dist}(0,W(A))/\|A\|_2$, then GMRES satisfies $$\|r_k\| \le \big(2 + \tfrac{2}{\sqrt3}\big)(2 + \gamma_\beta)\,\gamma_\beta^k\,\|r_0\|,\qquad \gamma_\beta = 2\sin\Big(\frac{\beta}{4 - 2\beta/\pi}\Big) < \sin\beta,$$ improving Elman's $\|r_k\| \le \sin^k\beta\,\|r_0\|$ in rate.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$ (or real, via complexification) with $0 \notin W(A)$

mathlib_prereqs.note: See field-of-values-def.

results.notes: Assume. The constant 2 + 2/√3 comes from a lens-shaped (lenticular) von Neumann-type inequality of Beckermann–Crouzeix, not from Crouzeix–Palencia; proving it needs that inequality and a Faber-polynomial construction. Real A: the real GMRES residual equals the complex one (see gmres-def notes). Consumers: non-normal preconditioned solves whose field of values is controlled (e.g. sketch-preconditioned nonsymmetric systems), comparison with gmres-elman.

results.title: Greenbaum–Pták–Strakoš: any nonincreasing GMRES curve is possible
results.informal: Given $f(0) \ge f(1) \ge \dots \ge f(n-1) > 0$ and any nonzero $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n \in \mathbb C$, there are $A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ and $b$ such that GMRES from $x_0 = 0$ has $\|r_k\| = f(k)$ for $k = 0,\dots,n-1$. Eigenvalues alone say nothing about GMRES for non-normal $A$.
results.conclusion: $\exists A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}, b \in \mathbb C^n$: $\operatorname{charpoly}A = \prod_i(x - \lambda_i)$ and the GMRES residuals with $x_0 = 0$ satisfy $\|r_k\| = f(k)$, $0 \le k \le n-1$

mathlib_prereqs.note: No companion-matrix API; the construction uses A = W C W⁻¹ with C a companion matrix and W built from an orthonormal basis.

results.notes: A caution, not a tool: it explains why gmres-diagonalizable needs κ(V) and why field-of-values bounds exist. The construction is explicit (Arioli–Pták–Strakoš 1998 parametrisation), so it is provable at difficulty 3 once complex GMRES exists. No downstream consumers; include for the record. Prove (later).

results.title: Lanczos-FA error: ‖f(A)b − Q f(T) Qᵀb‖ ≤ 2‖b‖ min_p ‖f − p‖
results.informal: For symmetric $A$ with spectrum in $[\lambda_{lo},\lambda_{hi}]$, $Q$ with orthonormal columns and $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$, and $T = Q^\top AQ$, $$\|f(A)b - Q\,f(T)\,Q^\top b\| \le 2\|b\|\min_{\deg p < q}\ \max_{x\in[\lambda_{lo},\lambda_{hi}]}|f(x) - p(x)|$$ for every $f : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ ($f(A)$ by the spectral calculus). For Lanczos, $Q^\top b = \|b\|e_1$, giving $\|b\|\,Q_qf(T_q)e_1$.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric with every eigenvalue in $[\lambda_{lo},\lambda_{hi}]$
$Q \in \mathbb R^{n\times k}$, $Q^\top Q = I$, $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$, $q \ge 1$, $T = Q^\top AQ$
$f : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$, $p$ with $\deg p < q$ and $|f - p| \le E$ on $[\lambda_{lo},\lambda_{hi}]$
results.notes: Proof: f(A)b − Qf(T)Qᵀb = (f − p)(A)b − Q(f − p)(T)Qᵀb by exactness, each term ≤ E‖b‖ since Ritz values lie in [λ_lo, λ_hi] (`eigenvalues_transpose_mul_mul_mem_Icc` already proved) and ‖Q‖ ≤ 1. The vector analogue of the proved quadrature error `abs_dotProduct_cfc_mulVec_sub_le_of_krylovSpace_le`. Combine with `inverse-polynomial-approx` (f = 1/x), `bernstein-ellipse-approx` (analytic f), and T2's exp / x^{−1/2} / sign approximations. Consumers: Krylov-aware trace estimation of f(A) (Chen–Hallman 2023), sampling N(0, A) via A^{1/2}b, matrix-exponential actions in randomized network centrality, block Lanczos for tr f(A) in `slq-error`-type results. Prove.

results.title: Arnoldi-FA error via the field of values: 2(1+√2) times best approximation on W(A)
results.informal: For any $A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $Q$ with orthonormal columns and $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$, $H = Q^*AQ$, and polynomials $g$ (any degree) and $p$ with $\deg p < q$ and $|g - p| \le E$ on $W(A)$: $$\|g(A)b - Q\,g(H)\,Q^*b\| \le 2(1+\sqrt2)\,E\,\|b\|.$$ By density this extends to $f$ holomorphic near $W(A)$ once a holomorphic functional calculus is available.
hypotheses: $A \in \mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $b \in \mathbb C^n$, $Q^*Q = I$, $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$, $H = Q^*AQ$
$g, p \in \mathbb C[x]$, $\deg p < q$, $\sup_{z\in W(A)}|g(z) - p(z)| \le E$

mathlib_prereqs.decl: holomorphic functional calculus for non-normal matrices
mathlib_prereqs.note: Mathlib's `cfc` needs IsStarNormal over ℂ; no Riesz–Dunford calculus for general matrices, hence the polynomial-g formulation.
The matrix exponential is available, so f = exp can be reached by truncating its series.

results.notes: Uses W(H) ⊆ W(A) (compression) and crouzeix-palencia for both A and H. Requires the complex Krylov space (see krylov-grade notes). With Crouzeix's conjectured constant 2 the factor would be 4. Consumers: exponential integrators and non-symmetric network-centrality / trace estimators. Prove modulo the assumed crouzeix-palencia.

results.title: Angle between the top eigenvector and the Krylov space (Chebyshev bound)
aliases: distance of an eigenvector to K_q
results.informal: For symmetric $A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_n$, $\lambda_2 > \lambda_n$, unit eigenvector $u_1$, and $\langle u_1,b\rangle \ne 0$, the vector $x = T_{q-1}\big(\tfrac{2A - (\lambda_2+\lambda_n)I}{\lambda_2-\lambda_n}\big)b \in \mathcal K_q(A,b)$ satisfies $$\tan\angle(u_1,x) \le \frac{\tan\angle(u_1,b)}{T_{q-1}(1+2\gamma)},\qquad \gamma = \frac{\lambda_1-\lambda_2}{\lambda_2-\lambda_n},$$ where $\tan\angle(u,x) = \|(I - uu^\top)x\|/|\langle u,x\rangle|$; and $T_{q-1}(1+2\gamma) \ge \tfrac12(1+2\gamma+2\sqrt{\gamma+\gamma^2})^{q-1}$.
results.conclusion: $\exists x \in \mathcal K_q(A,b)$ with $\langle u_1,x\rangle \ne 0$ and $\|(I - u_1u_1^\top)x\|/|\langle u_1,x\rangle| \le \dfrac{\|(I - u_1u_1^\top)b\|/|\langle u_1,b\rangle|}{T_{q-1}(1+2\gamma)}$
results.notes: The gap-dependent counterpart of the proved gap-free `ritz-value-bounds` (which uses the Chebyshev amplifier and pays ε λ_1). The general form for u_i with the factor κ_i = ∏_{j<i}(λ_j − λ_n)/(λ_j − λ_i) and T_{q−i}(1+2γ_i) is a later variant. Consumers: kaniel-paige-saad, `random-start-power` (Kuczyński–Woźniakowski gap-dependent rate with a Gaussian start, where tan²∠(u_1, g) is controlled by `chi-square-*`), the gap-dependent block Krylov/subspace-iteration bounds (`block-krylov-lra`, `subspace-iteration-expected`), Davis–Kahan-type eigenvector guarantees for PCA. Prove.

results.title: Kaniel–Paige–Saad bound for the largest Ritz value
results.informal: Under the hypotheses of krylov-eigenvector-angle, the largest Ritz value $\theta_1 = \lambda_{\max}(Q^\top AQ)$ for any $Q$ with orthonormal columns and $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$ satisfies $$0 \le \lambda_1 - \theta_1 \le (\lambda_1 - \lambda_n)\Big(\frac{\tan\angle(u_1,b)}{T_{q-1}(1+2\gamma)}\Big)^2,\qquad \gamma = \frac{\lambda_1-\lambda_2}{\lambda_2-\lambda_n}.$$
hypotheses: $Q \in \mathbb R^{n\times k}$ with $Q^\top Q = I$ and $\mathcal K_q(A,b) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$; $\theta_1$ the largest eigenvalue of $Q^\top AQ$
results.notes: Proof: θ_1 ≥ Rayleigh quotient of the x from krylov-eigenvector-angle (Courant–Fischer on QᵀAQ), and λ_1 − xᵀAx/xᵀx ≤ (λ_1 − λ_n) sin²∠(u_1,x) ≤ (λ_1 − λ_n) tan²∠; θ_1 ≤ λ_1 by interlacing. The existing `ritz-value-bounds` cites saad11 Thm 6.4 but proves the gap-free variant; this entry is the statement that label refers to. General i-th Ritz value form (with κ_i) later. Consumers: `random-start-power` (Lanczos clause), block-krylov-lra (per-vector gap-dependent bounds), spectral-norm estimation by Lanczos with a random start. Prove.

results.title: Polynomial-filtered range finder: HMT Thm 9.1 with test matrix φ(AᵀA)Ω
results.informal: Let $A = U_1\Sigma_1V_1^\top + U_2\Sigma_2V_2^\top$ be a block SVD ($[V_1\ V_2]$ orthogonal, $\Sigma_1 \in \mathbb R^{k\times k}$), $\Omega_i = V_i^\top\Omega$, and $\varphi$ a real polynomial with $\varphi(\sigma_j^2) \ne 0$ for $j \le k$. If $Q$ has orthonormal columns with $\operatorname{range}(\varphi(AA^\top)A\Omega) \subseteq \operatorname{range}Q$ and $\Omega_1$ has full row rank, then $$\|(I - QQ^\top)A\|^2 \le \|\Sigma_2\|^2 + \|\Sigma_2\,\varphi(\Sigma_2^\top\Sigma_2)\,\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\,\varphi(\Sigma_1^2)^{-1}\|^2,$$ and the same in the Frobenius norm. Hence $\|(I-QQ^\top)A\|^2 \le \sigma_{k+1}^2 + \big(\max_{j>k}\sigma_j|\varphi(\sigma_j^2)|\,/\,\min_{j\le k}|\varphi(\sigma_j^2)|\big)^2\|\Omega_2\|^2\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|^2$. Since $\varphi(AA^\top)A\Omega \in \mathcal K_q(AA^\top, A\Omega)$ for $\deg\varphi < q$, this holds for the block Krylov basis with every such $\varphi$ simultaneously.

$\Omega \in \mathbb R^{n\times s}$, $\Omega_1 = V_1^\top\Omega$ full row rank, $\Omega_2 = V_2^\top\Omega$

results.title: Chebyshev coefficients and Chebyshev truncation
results.informal: For $f$ continuous on $[-1,1]$, $a_k(f) = \tfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(\cos\theta)\cos(k\theta)\,d\theta$ for $k \ge 1$ (with $\tfrac{1}{\pi}$ for $k=0$) and the Chebyshev truncation is $f_n = \sum_{k \le n} a_k(f)\,T_k$. Characterised by the weighted inner product $\int f T_k (1-x^2)^{-1/2}$, exact on polynomials, and bounded by $2\max_{[-1,1]}|f|$.
results.conclusion: $a_k(f) = \tfrac{2}{\pi}\int_{-1}^{1} f(x)T_k(x)(1-x^2)^{-1/2}\,dx$ for $k \ge 1$ ($\tfrac{1}{\pi}$ for $k = 0$); $f \mapsto a_k(f)$ is linear; $a_k(T_m) = \delta_{km}$; if $\deg p \le n$ then $a_k(p) = 0$ for $k > n$ and $p_n = \sum_{k \le n} a_k(p)\,T_k = p$; $|a_0(f)| \le \max_{[-1,1]}|f|$ and $|a_k(f)| \le 2\max_{[-1,1]}|f|$

results.title: Bernstein ellipse
results.informal: For $\rho > 1$, $E_\rho = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z-1| + |z+1| < \rho + \rho^{-1}\}$, the open region bounded by the ellipse with foci $\pm 1$ and semi-axis sum $\rho$; equivalently the Joukowski image $\{(w + w^{-1})/2 : \rho^{-1} < |w| < \rho\}$. On $[a,b]$ one uses its affine image with foci $a, b$.
hypotheses: for the interval version: $a < b$ and $\varphi(t) = \tfrac{(b-a)t + (b+a)}{2}$
results.conclusion: $E_\rho$ is open, increasing in $\rho$ and contains $[-1,1]$; $E_\rho = J(\{\rho^{-1} < |w| < \rho\})$ with $J(w) = (w + w^{-1})/2$; every $z \in \overline{E_\rho}$ has $|z| \le \tfrac{\rho+\rho^{-1}}{2}$ and $\operatorname{Re} z \ge -\tfrac{\rho+\rho^{-1}}{2}$; $|T_n(z)| \le \tfrac{\rho^n + \rho^{-n}}{2}$ on $\overline{E_\rho}$; every $z \in \varphi(\overline{E_\rho})$ has $\operatorname{Re} z \ge \tfrac{(b+a) - (b-a)(\rho+\rho^{-1})/2}{2}$ and $|z| \le \tfrac{|b+a| + (b-a)(\rho+\rho^{-1})/2}{2}$

results.title: Best uniform approximation error E_n(f; [a,b])
results.informal: $E_n(f;[a,b]) = \inf\{E : \exists p,\ \deg p \le n,\ |f - p| \le E \text{ on } [a,b]\}$, written as an `sInf` in the `IsLeast` style of `isLeast_chebyshev_minimax`. For continuous $f$ the infimum is attained, decreases to $0$ (Weierstrass), and is invariant under affine change of variable.
results.conclusion: there is $p^*$ with $\deg p^* \le n$ and $\max_{[a,b]}|f - p^*| = E_n(f)$; $E_{n+1}(f) \le E_n(f) \le \max_{[a,b]}|f|$ and $E_n(f) \to 0$; $E_n(f + p) = E_n(f)$ for $\deg p \le n$, $E_n(cf) = |c|\,E_n(f)$, $E_n(f+g) \le E_n(f) + E_n(g)$; $E_n(f;[a,b]) = E_n(f\circ\varphi;[-1,1])$ for the affine bijection $\varphi : [-1,1] \to [a,b]$

results.informal: On the Chebyshev grid $x_j = \cos(j\pi/n)$, $T_m$, $T_{2n\pm m}$, $T_{4n\pm m}, \dots$ take the same values; hence the interpolant $p_n$ has coefficients $c_k = a_k + \sum_{\ell \ge 1}(a_{2\ell n + k} + a_{2\ell n - k})$ and $\max|f - p_n| \le 2\sum_{k>n}|a_k|$.

results.title: Chebyshev equioscillation theorem (ATAP Thm 10.1)
results.informal: A continuous real $f$ on $[a,b]$ has a unique best approximation $p^* \in \mathcal{P}_n$, and $p$ with $\deg p \le n$ is $p^*$ iff $f - p$ equioscillates at $n+2$ points: $a \le x_0 < \cdots < x_{n+1} \le b$ with $f(x_i) - p(x_i) = \sigma(-1)^i\max_{[a,b]}|f - p|$.
results.conclusion: $\max_{[a,b]}|f - p| = E_n(f;[a,b])$ if and only if there are $a \le x_0 < \cdots < x_{n+1} \le b$ and $\sigma \in \{\pm 1\}$ with $f(x_i) - p(x_i) = \sigma(-1)^i\max_{[a,b]}|f - p|$ for all $i$; the best approximation is unique

results.title: De la Vallée Poussin lower bound for best approximation
results.informal: If $f - p$ ($\deg p \le n$) takes nonzero values of alternating sign at $n+2$ points of $[a,b]$, every polynomial of degree $\le n$ has error at least $\min_i |f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$ at one of those points, so $E_n(f) \ge \min_i|f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$.
hypotheses: $p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le n$ and $(f(x_i) - p(x_i))(f(x_{i+1}) - p(x_{i+1})) < 0$ for $0 \le i \le n$
results.conclusion: for every $q \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg q \le n$, $\max_{0 \le i \le n+1}|f(x_i) - q(x_i)| \ge \min_{0 \le i \le n+1}|f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$; hence $E_n(f;[a,b]) \ge \min_i|f(x_i) - p(x_i)|$
results.notes: Proof: if q beat the minimum at every x_i, q - p would have the sign of f - p at the n+2 points, hence n+1 roots, hence q = p: contradiction.
