Consumers: spectral density estimation by SLQ (ctu21) and by moment matching (bkm22), eigenvalue counts with Lipschitz-smoothed indicators. Prove once jackson-lipschitz is assumed.

results.title: Low-degree approximation of x^s (Sachdeva–Vishnoi Thm 3.3)
results.informal: $x^s = \sum_{j=0}^{s} 2^{-s}\binom{s}{j}T_{|s-2j|}(x)$; keeping the terms with $|s - 2j| \le d$ gives $p_{s,d}$ of degree $\le d$ with $\max_{[-1,1]}|x^s - p_{s,d}| \le 2e^{-d^2/(2s)}$, so degree $\sqrt{2s\log(2/\varepsilon)}$ suffices for error $\varepsilon$.
results.conclusion: $x^s = \sum_{j=0}^{s} 2^{-s}\binom{s}{j}\,T_{|s-2j|}(x)$ as polynomials, and $p_{s,d} = \sum_{j\,:\,|s-2j| \le d} 2^{-s}\binom{s}{j}\,T_{|s-2j|}$ has $\deg p_{s,d} \le d$ and $|x^s - p_{s,d}(x)| \le 2e^{-d^2/(2s)}$ for $x \in [-1,1]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: 2 T_m T_k = T_{m+k} + T_{m-k}; with m = 1 gives x T_k = (T_{k+1} + T_{k-1})/2
Chernoff bound for the binomial tail

results.notes: The binomial tail Σ_{|s-2j|>d} 2^{-s} C(s,j) ≤ 2e^{-d²/(2s)} is proved from Σ_j C(s,j) e^{λ(s-2j)} = (2 cosh λ)^s and `Real.cosh_le_exp_half_sq`, without probability (Polynomial is layer 0 and cannot import Concentration). Consumers: exp-polynomial-approx; the 'Lanczos with q steps matches power iteration with q² steps' comparison behind random-start-power (kw92) and block Krylov vs subspace iteration (mm15); polynomial approximation of matrix powers. Prove.

results.title: Polynomial approximation of e^{-x} on [0,b] (Sachdeva–Vishnoi Thm 4.1)
results.informal: For $b > 0$ and $0 < \delta \le 1$, with $t = \lceil\max(e^2 b/2, \log(2/\delta))\rceil$ and $d = \lceil\sqrt{2t\log(4/\delta)}\rceil$, some $p$ of degree $\le d$ has $|e^{-x} - p(x)| \le \delta$ on $[0,b]$: degree $O\big(\sqrt{\max(b, \log(1/\delta))\log(1/\delta)}\big)$ with the constants shown. For $e^{-\tau x}$ on $[0,\beta]$ take $b = \tau\beta$.
results.conclusion: $\exists p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le d$ and $|e^{-x} - p(x)| \le \delta$ for all $x \in [0,b]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Taylor remainder only for |x| ≤ 1; the Poisson tail Σ_{i≥t}(b/2)^i/i! ≤ e^{b/2}(eb/(2t))^t must be proved

results.notes: Constants derived here following the SV proof (SV state the degree with O(·)): write e^{-x} = e^{-b/2}e^{-(b/2)y}, y = 2x/b - 1; truncate the Taylor series at t terms (tail ≤ (eb/(2t))^t ≤ e^{-t} ≤ δ/2); replace each y^i, 1 ≤ i < t, by p_{i,d} at total cost ≤ 2e^{-d²/(2t)} ≤ δ/2. Consumers: tr exp(-τA) (heat-kernel trace, Estrada index) by SLQ / Hutch++, exp(-τA)b by Lanczos (Musco–Musco–Sidford 2018), matrix multiplicative weights; optimality in exp-approx-lower-bound. Prove.

results.title: Degree lower bound for approximating e^{-x} on [0,b]
results.informal: If $\deg p \le q$ and $|p - e^{-x}| \le \delta \le 1/8$ on $[0,b]$ with $b \ge 1$, then $q^2 \ge \dfrac{(1 - e^{-1} - 2\delta)\,b}{2(1+\delta)}$; in particular $q \ge \sqrt{b/6}$.
hypotheses: $p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le q$ and $|p(x) - e^{-x}| \le \delta$ for $x \in [0,b]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: mean value theorem on [0,1]

results.notes: Constants derived here: the MVT on [0,1] gives |p'(ξ)| ≥ 1 - e^{-1} - 2δ; Markov on [0,b] (NLAlib `abs_eval_derivative_le_two_mul_sq_div_mul_of_forall_abs_eval_le`) gives |p'(ξ)| ≤ 2q²(1+δ)/b. Shows the √b in exp-polynomial-approx is optimal. Consumers: optimality claims for Lanczos/Chebyshev exp(A)b and heat-trace estimation. Prove.

results.title: Approximation on [a,b] of functions analytic in the right half-plane (x^{-1/2}, log x, x^alpha)
results.informal: For $0 < a < b$, $\rho_0 = \tfrac{\sqrt b + \sqrt a}{\sqrt b - \sqrt a}$ and $1 < r < \rho_0$, the transplanted ellipse $\varphi(E_r)$ lies in $\{\operatorname{Re} z \ge m_r\}$ with $m_r = \tfrac{(b+a) - (b-a)(r + r^{-1})/2}{2} > 0$. So any $F$ analytic on $\operatorname{Re} z > 0$ with $|F| \le M$ there is approximated on $[a,b]$ to within $\tfrac{2Mr^{-n}}{r-1}$ by degree $n$; $M = \max(m_r^\alpha, R_r^\alpha)$ for $x^\alpha$ and $\max(|\log m_r|, |\log R_r|) + \pi/2$ for $\log x$.
hypotheses: $0 < a < b$, $\rho_0 = \tfrac{\sqrt b + \sqrt a}{\sqrt b - \sqrt a}$, $1 < r < \rho_0$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$
$F$ complex-differentiable on $\{\operatorname{Re} z > 0\}$, real on $[a,b]$, with $|F(z)| \le M$ whenever $\operatorname{Re} z \ge m_r$ and $|z| \le R_r$
results.conclusion: $m_r > 0$ and $\exists p$ with $\deg p \le n$ and $|F(x) - p(x)| \le \dfrac{2Mr^{-n}}{r - 1}$ for $x \in [a,b]$; for $F(z) = z^{\alpha}$ ($\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$) one may take $M = \max(m_r^{\alpha}, R_r^{\alpha})$, for $F = \operatorname{Log}$, $M = \max(|\log m_r|, |\log R_r|) + \pi/2$

mathlib_prereqs.note: NLAlib, not Mathlib: (b+a)/(b-a) + √(((b+a)/(b-a))² - 1) = (√b+√a)/(√b-√a), the same ρ₀

results.notes: r ↑ ρ₀ trades constant for rate; degree O(√κ log(κ/ε)) for x^{-1/2} and log. For 1/x it is weaker than NLAlib's inverse-polynomial-approx (variant). Consumers: slq-error with f = log (log-determinant, ucs17) and f = x^{-1/2}; Krylov methods for A^{-1/2}b (Gaussian sampling, whitening); sign-polynomial-approx; T1's Krylov f(A)b bounds for Stieltjes-type f. Prove.

results.title: Polynomial approximation of sign(x) away from 0
results.informal: For $0 < \gamma < 1$ and $1 < r < \tfrac{1+\gamma}{1-\gamma}$ there is an odd $p(x) = x\,q(x^2)$ of degree $\le 2n+1$ with $|\operatorname{sgn} x - p(x)| \le \tfrac{2m_r^{-1/2}r^{-n}}{r-1}$ for $\gamma \le |x| \le 1$ (the $x^{-1/2}$ bound on $[\gamma^2, 1]$). With $r = 1 + \gamma$ the bound is $\tfrac{4}{\sqrt3\,\gamma^2}(1+\gamma)^{-n}$: degree $O(\gamma^{-1}\log(1/(\gamma\varepsilon)))$. The step $\mathbf{1}[x \ge c]$ is $(1 + \operatorname{sgn}(x - c))/2$.
results.conclusion: $\exists q$ with $\deg q \le n$ such that $p(x) = x\,q(x^2)$ satisfies $|\operatorname{sgn}(x) - p(x)| \le \dfrac{2\,m_r^{-1/2}\,r^{-n}}{r - 1}$ for $\gamma \le |x| \le 1$; for $r = 1+\gamma$, $m_r = \gamma^2(3+\gamma)/4$ and the bound is at most $\dfrac{4}{\sqrt3\,\gamma^2}(1+\gamma)^{-n}$
results.notes: As r ↑ (1+γ)/(1-γ) the base per degree-2 step tends to (1-γ)/(1+γ), the exponential base of Eremenko–Yuditskii's sharp asymptotics (EY07 Thm 1; pin its exact constant before adding it as an assumed variant). A variant with |p| ≤ 1 on all of [-1,1] (needed for stable projector polynomials; Gilyén–Su–Low–Wiebe 2019) is later. Consumers: spectral projectors and principal component projection/regression (fmms16), eigenvalue counting in an interval (spectral density), gap-dependent block Krylov. Lower bound: sign-approx-lower-bound. Prove.

results.title: Degree lower bound for approximating sign(x) with a gap
results.informal: If $\deg p \le q$, $|p| \le M$ on $[-1,1]$ and $|p - \operatorname{sgn}| \le \varepsilon < 1$ on $\gamma \le |x| \le 1$, then $qM \ge \dfrac{(1-\varepsilon)\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}}{\gamma}$.
hypotheses: $p \in \mathbb{R}[x]$ with $\deg p \le q$ and $|p(x)| \le M$ for $x \in [-1,1]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: mean value theorem on [-γ, γ]

results.notes: Derivation: the MVT on [-γ,γ] gives ξ with p'(ξ) ≥ (1-ε)/γ; Bernstein (NLAlib `abs_eval_derivative_le_div_sqrt_of_forall_abs_eval_le`) gives |p'(ξ)| ≤ qM/√(1-γ²). Shows the 1/γ order in sign-polynomial-approx is optimal. Consumers: optimality of gap-dependent Krylov and projector rates. Prove.

results.title: Lower bound for polynomial approximation of 1/x on [a,b]
results.informal: If $\deg p < q$ and $|p(x) - 1/x| \le \varepsilon$ on $[a,b]$, then $\varepsilon \ge \tfrac{1}{b}\big(\tfrac{\sqrt b - \sqrt a}{\sqrt b + \sqrt a}\big)^q$; `inverse-polynomial-approx` is sharp up to the factor $2b/a$.
results.notes: Proof: r = 1 - x p has degree ≤ q, r(0) = 1 and |r| ≤ bε on [a,b]; apply NLAlib `inv_eval_T_real_le_of_forall_abs_eval_le`, then `eval_T_real_le_pow` with `add_div_sub_add_sqrt_sq_sub_one_eq`. Consumers: optimality of the √κ rates of CG, Chebyshev iteration and Lanczos solves; lower bounds on iteration counts in sketch-and-precondition. Prove.

results.title: Majorization and weak majorization of real vectors
results.informal: For $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$ write $s_k(x)=\sum_{i\le k}x_i^\downarrow$ for the sum of the $k$ largest entries. $x\prec_w y$ (weak majorization) iff $s_k(x)\le s_k(y)$ for $k=1,\dots,n$; $x\prec y$ iff moreover $s_n(x)=s_n(y)$. Characterisations: $x\prec y$ iff $x=Dy$ for a doubly stochastic $D$ iff $x\in\operatorname{conv}\{Py: P \text{ a permutation}\}$ (Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya); $x\prec y$ iff $\sum_i\varphi(x_i)\le\sum_i\varphi(y_i)$ for every convex $\varphi$; $x\prec_w y$ iff the same holds for every increasing convex $\varphi$.
hypotheses: $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^n$ (index type `Fin n`, or any `Fintype` index)
For the function characterisations: $\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ convex (increasing and convex for $\prec_w$)
results.conclusion: $x\prec y \iff \exists D \text{ doubly stochastic},\ x = Dy \iff \forall\varphi \text{ convex},\ \sum_i\varphi(x_i)\le\sum_i\varphi(y_i)$; and $x\prec_w y\iff\forall\varphi$ increasing convex, $\sum_i\varphi(x_i)\le\sum_i\varphi(y_i)$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Submonoid of doubly stochastic matrices (Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.DoublyStochasticMatrix).
Birkhoff's theorem; turns the doubly-stochastic form into the convex-hull form.
Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Birkhoff.lean lists the HLP characterisation as a TODO; no definition exists.
Jensen, for the (⇒) direction of the convex-function form.

results.notes: Lean design: avoid sorting by defining the top-k sum as a maximum over k-subsets, s_k(x) = sup over Finset.powersetCard k univ of ∑_{i∈S} x_i; this is index-type agnostic and matches how Ky Fan sums are proved. Consumers: schur-horn, lidskii, unitarily-invariant-norm-def (Fan dominance), horn-product-inequality, schatten-norms-def; downstream the Wasserstein-type spectrum comparisons used for spectral density (slq-error). Recommendation: prove the definition, the doubly-stochastic (⇐) direction and the convex-function (⇒) direction (difficulty 2); the (⇒) HLP direction is the hard part (difficulty 3–4) and can be assumed if a consumer needs it first. Labels in mo11 to verify against the printed edition.

results.title: Ky Fan maximum principle for eigenvalue and singular-value sums
aliases: sum of top-k eigenvalues as max trace
results.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$ and $0\le k\le n$: $$\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i(A)=\max\{\operatorname{tr}(Q^\top AQ): Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times k},\ Q^\top Q=I_k\},$$ attained at any $k$ orthonormal top eigenvectors (dually, the bottom $k$ sum is the minimum). For $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$: $\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(A)=\max\{\operatorname{tr}(U^\top AV): U^\top U=V^\top V=I_k\}$. Corollary: $\sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(A+B)\le\sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(A)+\sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(B)$, i.e. $\lambda(A+B)\prec\lambda(A)+\lambda(B)$, and $\sigma(A+B)\prec_w\sigma(A)+\sigma(B)$.
hypotheses: $A=A^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, eigenvalues in decreasing order (`eigenvalues₀`)
Singular-value form: $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $U\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}$, $V\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ with orthonormal columns, $k\le\min(m,n)$
results.conclusion: $\operatorname{tr}(Q^\top AQ)\le\sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(A)$ with equality for top eigenvectors; $\operatorname{tr}(U^\top AV)\le\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(A)$ with equality for top singular vectors

mathlib_prereqs.note: Sorted (antitone) eigenvalues.
NLAlib.singularValues is bridged to it.

results.notes: Proof route with what NLAlib already has: tr(QᵀAQ) = ∑ᵢ λᵢ(QᵀAQ) ≤ ∑_{i≤k} λᵢ(A) by the compression half of Cauchy interlacing (NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_compression_le), equality at eigenvectors; the singular-value form is von Neumann (NLAlib.frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul) applied to ⟨A, UVᵀ⟩, since UVᵀ has k unit singular values. Consumers: ky-fan-norms-def (triangle inequality), schur-horn (Schur half is immediate: take Q = coordinate vectors), lidskii, eigenvalue sums in PCA/subspace objectives, block-krylov-lra (MM15's per-vector and Ky Fan error guarantees), nystrom-randomized and hutchpp (trace of the top-k part). Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Ky Fan k-norms and the nuclear norm
results.informal: $\|A\|_{(k)}=\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(A)$ and $\|A\|_*=\sum_i\sigma_i(A)=\|A\|_{(\min(m,n))}$. Characterisations: each $\|\cdot\|_{(k)}$ is a norm on $\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, invariant under $A\mapsto UAV$ for orthogonal $U,V$ and under transpose; $\|A\|_{(1)}=\|A\|$; $\|A\|_*=\max\{\langle A,B\rangle_F:\|B\|\le1\}$ (duality with the spectral norm); $\|A\|_*=\operatorname{tr}A$ for $A\succeq0$; $\|A\|\le\|A\|_*\le\operatorname{rank}(A)\|A\|$ and $\|A\|_F\le\|A\|_*\le\sqrt{\operatorname{rank}A}\,\|A\|_F$.
results.conclusion: $\|\cdot\|_{(k)}$ and $\|\cdot\|_*$ are orthogonally invariant norms with $\|A\|_{(1)}=\|A\|$, $\|A\|_*=\max_{\|B\|\le1}\langle A,B\rangle_F$, $\|A\|_*=\operatorname{tr}A$ for $A\succeq0$, and the stated comparisons with $\|A\|$, $\|A\|_F$

mathlib_prereqs.note: No trace-class or Schatten norm on matrices in Mathlib.

results.notes: TARGETING.md §3 already lists the nuclear norm as part of the wanted MatrixAnalysis_basic bundle; nystrom-randomized states its error in the nuclear norm and von-neumann-trace's corollary is phrased with ‖X‖_*. Consumers: nystrom-randomized, hutchpp, von-neumann-rank-bound, unitarily-invariant-norm-def (Fan dominance), lidskii (UI-norm corollary), schatten-norms-def. Recommendation: prove (triangle inequality from the max principle; duality from von Neumann + SVD).

results.title: Schatten p-norms and the matrix Hölder inequality
results.informal: $\|A\|_{S_p}=\big(\sum_i\sigma_i(A)^p\big)^{1/p}$ for $1\le p<\infty$, $\|A\|_{S_\infty}=\sigma_1(A)$. Characterisations: $S_1$ nuclear, $S_2$ Frobenius, $S_\infty$ spectral; each is an orthogonally invariant norm; Hölder $|\langle A,B\rangle_F|\le\|A\|_{S_p}\|B\|_{S_q}$ for $1/p+1/q=1$, and $\|AB\|_{S_r}\le\|A\|_{S_p}\|B\|_{S_q}$ for $1/r=1/p+1/q$; monotonicity $\|A\|_{S_q}\le\|A\|_{S_p}$ for $p\le q$ and $\|A\|_{S_p}\le\operatorname{rank}(A)^{1/p-1/q}\|A\|_{S_q}$.
hypotheses: $A,B$ real matrices of compatible sizes (`Fin` indices)
$1\le p,q,r\le\infty$ with the stated conjugacy relations
results.conclusion: $|\langle A,B\rangle_F|\le\|A\|_{S_p}\|B\|_{S_q}$; $\|AB\|_{S_r}\le\|A\|_{S_p}\|B\|_{S_q}$; $\|\cdot\|_{S_p}$ is a norm; the monotonicity and rank comparisons

mathlib_prereqs.note: Hölder for finite sequences; with von Neumann gives the trace Hölder inequality directly.

results.notes: Split when formalising: the trace Hölder inequality |⟨A,B⟩| ≤ ‖A‖_p‖B‖_q needs only von-neumann-trace + Real.inner_le_Lp_mul_Lq (difficulty 2, prove); the triangle inequality for general p needs the symmetric-gauge theory of unitarily-invariant-norm-def; the product Hölder needs horn-product-inequality. Consumers: Schatten-norm low-rank approximation bounds (tw23), trace-estimator variance in terms of ‖A‖_{S_2}, ‖A‖_{S_4} (hutchinson-variance), sketching for Schatten-norm estimation. Recommendation: prove Hölder now-ish, assume the norm property via Fan dominance.

results.title: Unitarily invariant norms: von Neumann's gauge characterisation and Fan dominance
results.informal: A norm on $\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ is orthogonally (unitarily) invariant if $\|UAV\|=\|A\|$ for all orthogonal $U,V$. (von Neumann) These are exactly $\|A\|=\Phi(\sigma(A))$ for a symmetric gauge function $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^{\min(m,n)}$, i.e. a norm invariant under permutations and sign changes. (Fan dominance) $\|A\|\le\|B\|$ for every orthogonally invariant norm iff $\|A\|_{(k)}\le\|B\|_{(k)}$ for every $k$, i.e. iff $\sigma(A)\prec_w\sigma(B)$.
hypotheses: $\|\cdot\|$ a norm on $\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $\|UAV\|=\|A\|$ for orthogonal $U\in O(m)$, $V\in O(n)$
results.conclusion: $\|A\|=\Phi(\sigma_1(A),\dots,\sigma_{\min(m,n)}(A))$ with $\Phi$ a symmetric gauge function, and conversely every symmetric gauge function defines such a norm; $\big(\forall\,\|\cdot\|\ \text{UI}:\ \|A\|\le\|B\|\big)\iff\forall k,\ \|A\|_{(k)}\le\|B\|_{(k)}$

sources.label: Thm IV.2.1 (von Neumann), Thm IV.2.2 (Fan dominance)

results.notes: Most randomized-NLA statements need only the spectral, Frobenius and nuclear norms, so this is a later foundation; it is what makes 'in every unitarily invariant norm' versions of eckart-young, weyl-mirsky (Mirsky 1960), davis-kahan-sin-theta and wedin-sin-theta one-line corollaries of a Ky Fan statement. Also absorbs the pinching inequality ‖∑ PᵢAPᵢ‖ ≤ ‖A‖ (Bhatia §IV.2, not proposed separately). Recommendation: prove the definition and the (⇒) direction of Fan dominance (trivial); assume the (⇐) direction (it needs the HLP direction of majorization-def).

results.title: Schur–Horn: the diagonal is majorized by the spectrum
results.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $(A_{11},\dots,A_{nn})\prec\lambda(A)$ (Schur), so $\sum_{i\in S}A_{ii}\le\sum_{i\le|S|}\lambda_i(A)$ for every index set $S$ and $\sum_i\varphi(A_{ii})\le\operatorname{tr}\varphi(A)$ for convex $\varphi$. Conversely (Horn) for every $d\prec\lambda$ there is a symmetric matrix with diagonal $d$ and spectrum $\lambda$ (a rotation of $\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)$).
results.conclusion: $\operatorname{diag}(A)\prec\lambda(A)$; and every $d\prec\lambda$ is $\operatorname{diag}(Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)Q^\top)$ for some orthogonal $Q$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Mathlib's Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Spectrum.lean cites Schur–Horn only as motivation for its decreasing-order convention.

results.notes: Schur's half is difficulty 2 (Ky Fan with Q = coordinate vectors, then majorization-def's convex-function form); Horn's converse is difficulty 4. Consumers: diagonal-estimator and trace estimation (∑A_ii² ≤ ∑λ_i², diagonal vs spectrum comparisons), rpcholesky (diagonal pivots against the spectrum, tr of Schur complements), leverage-scores (0 ≤ ℓ_i ≤ 1, ∑ℓ_i = rank is Schur for a projector), volume-sampling. Recommendation: prove Schur, assume Horn.

results.title: Lidskii–Wielandt: λ(A+B) − λ(A) ≺ λ(B), and Mirsky in every unitarily invariant norm
aliases: spectral variation in the nuclear norm
results.informal: For symmetric $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and every index set $J$ with $|J|=k$: $$\sum_{j\in J}\lambda_j(A+B)\le\sum_{j\in J}\lambda_j(A)+\sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i(B),$$ i.e. $\lambda(A+B)-\lambda(A)\prec\lambda(B)$. For singular values, $|\sigma(A+E)-\sigma(A)|\prec_w\sigma(E)$; hence $\|\operatorname{diag}(\sigma(A+E)-\sigma(A))\|\le\|E\|$ in every unitarily invariant norm, in particular $\sum_i|\lambda_i(A+E)-\lambda_i(A)|\le\|E\|_*$.
results.notes: NLAlib's weyl-mirsky already has the spectral (Weyl) and Frobenius (Mirsky) cases for singular values; Lidskii is the general-index-set statement behind all unitarily invariant cases. The nuclear-norm corollary gives the 1-Wasserstein bound between empirical spectral distributions, W₁ ≤ ‖A − B‖_*/n, used in spectral-density estimation (slq-error / ctu21-type analyses). Recommendation: assume (statement is textbook-certain; Wielandt's minimax proof is long).

results.title: Horn's product inequality and weak majorization of σ(AB)
aliases: log-majorization of singular values of a product
results.informal: For $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}$, $B\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ and every $k$: $\prod_{i\le k}\sigma_i(AB)\le\prod_{i\le k}\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(B)$ (Horn). Consequently (Weyl's majorant theorem) $\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(AB)^s\le\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(A)^s\sigma_i(B)^s$ for every $s>0$; in particular $\|AB\|_{(k)}\le\sum_{i\le k}\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(B)$.

mathlib_prereqs.note: Exterior powers exist, but compound matrices and σ(Λᵏ A) = products of σᵢ do not.

results.notes: The standard proof applies the k = 1 case to compound matrices; the additive corollary needs the log-majorization ⇒ weak majorization lemma (majorization-def with φ = exp). Consumers: schatten-norms-def (product Hölder), Schatten/nuclear-norm bounds of products in low-rank approximation (e.g. ‖Σ₂Ω₂Ω₁†‖_* in HMT-type nuclear bounds, nystrom-randomized), rsvd-tail. Recommendation: assume.

results.title: Weyl and Hoffman–Wielandt perturbation bounds for symmetric eigenvalues
aliases: von Neumann trace inequality for symmetric matrices
results.informal: For symmetric $A,E\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with decreasing eigenvalues: (Weyl) $\lambda_i(A)+\lambda_n(E)\le\lambda_i(A+E)\le\lambda_i(A)+\lambda_1(E)$, hence $|\lambda_i(A+E)-\lambda_i(A)|\le\|E\|$; (trace inequality) $\operatorname{tr}(AB)\le\sum_i\lambda_i(A)\lambda_i(B)$ for symmetric $A,B$; (Hoffman–Wielandt) $$\sum_i\big(\lambda_i(A+E)-\lambda_i(A)\big)^2\le\|E\|_F^2.$$
results.notes: weyl-mirsky covers singular values only; the symmetric-eigenvalue versions (which keep signs) are missing although NLAlib.eigenvalues₀_add_le (Weyl i+j) and eigenvalues₀_le_eigenvalues₀_of_posSemidef_sub (Loewner monotonicity) are there. Proof: Weyl from those two; the trace inequality by shifting A, B to PSD (eigenvalues = singular values) and von Neumann; Hoffman–Wielandt by expanding ‖(A+E) − A‖_F² and the trace inequality. Consumers: davis-kahan-sin-theta (population-gap corollary), slq-error and spectral-density bounds (W₂ distance between spectra ≤ ‖E‖_F/√n), ritz-value-bounds, nystrom-structural/nystrom-randomized eigenvalue statements, matrix-chernoff-sampling consequences, sketch-and-precondition (eigenvalues of AᵀSᵀSA). Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Weyl's multiplicative inequality σ_{i+j−1}(AB) ≤ σ_i(A)σ_j(B)
results.informal: For $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}$, $B\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ and $i,j\ge1$: $\sigma_{i+j-1}(AB)\le\sigma_i(A)\sigma_j(B)$. In NLAlib's 0-indexed convention: `singularValues (A * B) (i + j) ≤ singularValues A i * singularValues B j`. The case $j=1$ is $\sigma_i(AB)\le\sigma_i(A)\|B\|$.
results.notes: Additive companion NLAlib.singularValues_add_add_le already exists; the multiplicative one does not (only singularValues_mul_le_mul_specNorm / specNorm_mul). Proof: AB − [A_{i−1}B + (A − A_{i−1})B_{j−1}] = (A − A_{i−1})(B − B_{j−1}) with the bracket of rank ≤ i+j−2, then NLAlib.singularValues_le_specNorm_sub_of_rank_le. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Residual bounds for approximate eigenpairs (Krylov–Bogoliubov, Kato–Temple, one-vector sin θ)
aliases: quadratic accuracy of the Rayleigh quotient
results.informal: $A$ symmetric, $\|x\|=1$, $\rho=x^\top Ax$, $r=Ax-\rho x$. (a) For every $\mu\in\mathbb R$ some eigenvalue $\lambda$ satisfies $|\lambda-\mu|\le\|Ax-\mu x\|$; $\|r\|=\min_\mu\|Ax-\mu x\|$. (b) (Kato–Temple) if $\delta>0$ and $\lambda$ is the only eigenvalue in $(\rho-\delta,\rho+\delta)$ then $|\lambda-\rho|\le\|r\|^2/\delta$. (c) If $\delta=\min\{|\lambda'-\rho|:\lambda'\in\sigma(A)\setminus\{\lambda\}\}>0$ and $P_\lambda$ is the orthogonal projector onto the $\lambda$-eigenspace, $\|(I-P_\lambda)x\|\le\|r\|/\delta$. Also $\nabla_x\frac{x^\top Ax}{x^\top x}=\frac{2(Ax-\rho(x)x)}{x^\top x}$.

mathlib_prereqs.note: Gradient of x ↦ ⟪Tx, x⟫; the Rayleigh-quotient gradient follows.
Stationary points of the Rayleigh quotient are eigenvectors.

results.notes: Labels in parlett98 to verify. All three parts are a few lines from the spectral expansion x = ∑cᵢuᵢ (NLAlib.quadForm_eq_sum_eigenvalues, sum_sq_eigenvectorBasis_dotProduct). Consumers: ritz-value-bounds and Lanczos analysis (Ritz residual ‖r‖ = β_k|e_kᵀs|, needs lanczos-recurrence), random-start-power, power-method stopping criteria, T1's Kaniel–Paige–Saad bounds, LOBPCG/subspace-iteration stopping rules. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Spectrum, singular values and norms of Kronecker products
results.informal: If $A=U_A\Sigma_AV_A^\top$ and $B=U_B\Sigma_BV_B^\top$ then $A\otimes B=(U_A\otimes U_B)(\Sigma_A\otimes\Sigma_B)(V_A\otimes V_B)^\top$, so the singular values of $A\otimes B$ are $\{\sigma_i(A)\sigma_j(B)\}$; hence $\|A\otimes B\|=\|A\|\|B\|$, $\|A\otimes B\|_F=\|A\|_F\|B\|_F$, $\operatorname{rank}(A\otimes B)=\operatorname{rank}A\cdot\operatorname{rank}B$, $(A\otimes B)^\dagger=A^\dagger\otimes B^\dagger$. For symmetric $A,B$ the eigenvalues of $A\otimes B$ are $\lambda_i(A)\lambda_j(B)$ and those of $A\otimes I+I\otimes B$ are $\lambda_i(A)+\lambda_j(B)$.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$ (any `Fintype` indices; product index types)
results.conclusion: $\sigma(A\otimes B)=\{\sigma_i(A)\sigma_j(B)\}$ as multisets; $\|A\otimes B\|=\|A\|\|B\|$; $\|A\otimes B\|_F=\|A\|_F\|B\|_F$; $\operatorname{rank}(A\otimes B)=\operatorname{rank}A\operatorname{rank}B$; $(A\otimes B)^\dagger=A^\dagger\otimes B^\dagger$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Column-stacking vectorisation (Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Vec).
The vec trick vec(AXBᵀ) = (B ⊗ A) vec X.

mathlib_prereqs.decl: Singular values / norms / rank of a Kronecker product

Consumers: Kronecker/Khatri–Rao and tensor sketches (TensorSketch, Kronecker JL; not yet in the atlas), Kronecker-structured least squares, gaussian-frob-second-moment / gaussian-amm restated through vec and Kronecker covariance, Hutchinson with Kronecker-structured probes. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Canonical (principal) angles between subspaces and sin Θ
results.informal: For $Q,\hat Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ with orthonormal columns, the canonical angles $0\le\theta_1\le\dots\le\theta_k\le\pi/2$ are defined by $\cos\theta_i=\sigma_i(Q^\top\hat Q)$ (so $\|\sin\Theta\|=\sin\theta_k=\sqrt{1-\sigma_k(Q^\top\hat Q)^2}$), and $\sin\Theta(Q,\hat Q)=\operatorname{diag}(\sin\theta_i)$. Characterisations, with $Q_\perp$ an orthonormal complement of $Q$: $\|\sin\Theta\|=\|Q_\perp^\top\hat Q\|=\|(I-QQ^\top)\hat Q\|=\|QQ^\top-\hat Q\hat Q^\top\|$; $\|\sin\Theta\|_F^2=k-\|Q^\top\hat Q\|_F^2=\tfrac12\|QQ^\top-\hat Q\hat Q^\top\|_F^2$; $\Theta$ depends only on the ranges, is symmetric in $(Q,\hat Q)$; if $\theta_k<\pi/2$, $\|\tan\Theta\|=\|(Q_\perp^\top\hat Q)(Q^\top\hat Q)^{-1}\|$.
hypotheses: $Q,\hat Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ with $Q^\top Q=\hat Q^\top\hat Q=I_k$
results.conclusion: $\|\sin\Theta\|=\|Q_\perp^\top\hat Q\|=\|(I-QQ^\top)\hat Q\|=\|QQ^\top-\hat Q\hat Q^\top\|$, $\|\sin\Theta\|_F^2=k-\|Q^\top\hat Q\|_F^2=\tfrac12\|QQ^\top-\hat Q\hat Q^\top\|_F^2$, and the invariance/symmetry properties

mathlib_prereqs.note: Orthogonal projections onto submodules exist; angles between subspaces do not.

results.notes: State with matrices (HasOrthonormalCols) rather than submodules, as every consumer manipulates frames; give the submodule-level invariance as a lemma. Define the angles through NLAlib.singularValues (Qᵀ Q̂) on Fin k indices and expose ‖sin Θ‖ as specNorm (residual Q Q̂) so the projections API applies directly. Consumers: davis-kahan-sin-theta, wedin-sin-theta, pseudoinverse-perturbation (projector part), subspace-iteration-expected and block-krylov-lra (gap-dependent tan Θ forms), random-start-power (tan θ of the start vector), hmt-9-1-spectral (Ω₂Ω₁† is a tan Θ), leverage-score approximation from approximate bases. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Separation bound for the Sylvester operator X ↦ LX − XM
results.informal: Let $L\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, $M\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}$ be symmetric and $X\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$. (a) If $|\lambda_i(L)-\lambda_j(M)|\ge\delta>0$ for all $i,j$ then $\|LX-XM\|_F\ge\delta\|X\|_F$. (b) If the eigenvalues of $M$ lie in $[a,b]$ and those of $L$ lie outside $(a-\delta,b+\delta)$, $\delta>0$, then $\|LX-XM\|\ge\delta\|X\|$ (spectral norm; also Frobenius). The one-sided case $\lambda_{\max}(L)\le\alpha-\delta$, $\lambda_{\min}(M)\ge\alpha$ is the one used for top-$k$ subspaces.
hypotheses: $L=L^\top\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, $M=M^\top\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}$, $X\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$, $\delta>0$
results.notes: Engine of both sin θ theorems; keeping it separate lets Davis–Kahan and Wedin share it. (a) is entrywise after diagonalising L and M (difficulty 2). (b) in the spectral norm needs the interval/one-sided structure (with arbitrary interlaced spectra the best constant is π/2, Bhatia–Davis–McIntosh; do not state that). The one-sided case follows from a shift and a positivity argument. Labels in bhatia97 §VII.2 to verify. Consumers: davis-kahan-sin-theta, wedin-sin-theta, eigenvalue-residual-bounds (k = 1 case). Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Davis–Kahan sin Θ theorem for invariant subspaces of symmetric matrices
results.informal: $A,\hat A=A+E\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric. $Q_1\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ orthonormal with $AQ_1=Q_1\Lambda_1$; $[\hat Q_1\ \hat Q_2]$ orthogonal with $\hat A\hat Q_i=\hat Q_i\hat\Lambda_i$. If $\sigma(\Lambda_1)\subseteq[a,b]$ and $\sigma(\hat\Lambda_2)\cap(a-\delta,b+\delta)=\emptyset$ with $\delta>0$, then $$\|\sin\Theta(Q_1,\hat Q_1)\|=\|\hat Q_2^\top Q_1\|\le\frac{\|\hat Q_2^\top EQ_1\|}{\delta}\le\frac{\|EQ_1\|}{\delta}\le\frac{\|E\|}{\delta},$$ and the same with Frobenius norms. Top-$k$ corollary: with $Q_1,\hat Q_1$ top-$k$ eigenvectors, $\|\sin\Theta\|\le\|E\|/(\lambda_k(A)-\lambda_{k+1}(\hat A))$ when the denominator is positive. Population-gap form (Yu–Wang–Samworth): if $g=\lambda_k(A)-\lambda_{k+1}(A)>0$ then $\|\sin\Theta\|_F\le2\min(\sqrt k\|E\|,\|E\|_F)/g$ and $\|\sin\Theta\|\le2\|E\|/g$.
hypotheses: $Q_1\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}$ orthonormal, $AQ_1=Q_1\Lambda_1$; $[\hat Q_1\ \hat Q_2]$ orthogonal, $\hat A\hat Q_2=\hat Q_2\hat\Lambda_2$
results.notes: Proof: Q̂₂ᵀ(ÂQ₁ − Q₁Λ₁) = Λ̂₂(Q̂₂ᵀQ₁) − (Q̂₂ᵀQ₁)Λ₁ and ÂQ₁ − Q₁Λ₁ = EQ₁, then sylvester-separation-bound. The population-gap form: if ‖E‖ ≥ g/2 the bound is trivial (sin ≤ 1), otherwise Weyl (eigenvalue-perturbation-symmetric) gives λ_k(A) − λ_{k+1}(Â) ≥ g/2. Consumers: wedin-sin-theta; gap-dependent analyses of subspace-iteration-expected and block-krylov-lra; randomized PCA / spectral clustering from sketches; Nyström eigenvector accuracy (nystrom-randomized follow-ups); leverage scores of approximate eigenspaces (leverage-scores); random-start-power's gap form. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Wedin's sin Θ theorem for singular subspaces
results.informal: $A,\hat A=A+E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$; $U_1,V_1$ and $\hat U_1,\hat V_1$ the top-$k$ left/right singular vectors of $A$ and $\hat A$, $\hat\Sigma_1=\operatorname{diag}(\hat\sigma_1,\dots,\hat\sigma_k)$. With residuals $R=A\hat V_1-\hat U_1\hat\Sigma_1=-E\hat V_1$ and $S=A^\top\hat U_1-\hat V_1\hat\Sigma_1=-E^\top\hat U_1$, if $\delta:=\sigma_k(\hat A)-\sigma_{k+1}(A)>0$ then $$\max\{\|\sin\Theta(U_1,\hat U_1)\|,\|\sin\Theta(V_1,\hat V_1)\|\}\le\frac{\max\{\|R\|,\|S\|\}}{\delta}\le\frac{\|E\|}{\delta},$$ $$\sqrt{\|\sin\Theta(U_1,\hat U_1)\|_F^2+\|\sin\Theta(V_1,\hat V_1)\|_F^2}\le\frac{\sqrt{\|R\|_F^2+\|S\|_F^2}}{\delta}.$$ Population-gap form: if $g=\sigma_k(A)-\sigma_{k+1}(A)>0$ then both $\|\sin\Theta\|\le2\|E\|/g$.
hypotheses: $U_1,V_1$ (resp. $\hat U_1,\hat V_1$) orthonormal top-$k$ singular vectors of $A$ (resp. $\hat A$)
results.notes: Two routes: Wedin's direct proof with two coupled Sylvester bounds, or Davis–Kahan on the Hermitian dilation [[0, A], [Aᵀ, 0]] (whose eigenvectors are (u, ±v)/√2). NLAlib's hermitian-dilation is complex (NLAlib.dilation); a real dilation lemma is a small add-on. Population-gap corollary via NLAlib.singularValues_le_singularValues_add_add_specNorm (Weyl). Consumers: singular-vector accuracy of RSVD and sketched SVD, randomized low-rank approximation of singular subspaces (rsvd-tail follow-ups), matrix completion and spectral initialisation, leverage-score estimation from an approximate SVD (leverage-sampling-ose with approximate scores), sketched PCA. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Wedin's perturbation bounds for the pseudoinverse and range projectors
results.informal: $A,B=A+E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$. Identity: $$B^\dagger-A^\dagger=-B^\dagger EA^\dagger+B^\dagger B^{\dagger\top}E^\top(I-AA^\dagger)+(I-B^\dagger B)E^\top A^{\dagger\top}A^\dagger.$$ Bounds: if $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}B$ then $\|B^\dagger-A^\dagger\|\le\mu\|A^\dagger\|\|B^\dagger\|\|E\|$ with $\mu=\tfrac{1+\sqrt5}{2}$ (and $\|B^\dagger-A^\dagger\|_F\le\sqrt2\|A^\dagger\|\|B^\dagger\|\|E\|_F$); without the rank condition, $\|B^\dagger-A^\dagger\|\le\mu\max(\|A^\dagger\|^2,\|B^\dagger\|^2)\|E\|$. If $\operatorname{rank}A=\operatorname{rank}B$ and $\|A^\dagger\|\|E\|<1$: $\|B^\dagger\|\le\frac{\|A^\dagger\|}{1-\|A^\dagger\|\|E\|}$, and $\|AA^\dagger-BB^\dagger\|\le\min(\|A^\dagger\|,\|B^\dagger\|)\|E\|$.

mathlib_prereqs.note: Mathlib has no Moore–Penrose inverse; NLAlib's moorePenroseInverse is the definition to use.

results.notes: The identity is pure algebra from the four Penrose identities (NLAlib.IsMoorePenroseInverse). The simple constant μ = 3 is an immediate corollary (each term ≤ ‖B†‖‖E‖‖A†‖); the sharp (1+√5)/2 needs Wedin's orthogonality argument (difficulty 3–4). Labels and the μ table (3 for a general unitarily invariant norm, (1+√5)/2 spectral, √2 Frobenius) to verify against Stewart–Sun III.3.8 / Wedin 1973 before stating. Consumers: least-squares-perturbation, sketch-and-solve-ls and sketched-regression (stability of (SA)†), generalized Nyström stability (nakatsukasa20), sketch-and-precondition stability. Recommendation: prove the identity and μ = 3 form; assume the sharp constant if a consumer needs it.

results.title: Generalized Schur complement criterion for positive semidefinite block matrices
results.informal: For symmetric $M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^\top&C\end{pmatrix}$ with $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$: $$M\succeq0\iff A\succeq0,\ (I-AA^\dagger)B=0,\ C-B^\top A^\dagger B\succeq0.$$ When $M\succeq0$, the Schur complement $M/A=C-B^\top A^\dagger B$ satisfies $x^\top(M/A)x=\min_{y}\begin{pmatrix}y\\x\end{pmatrix}^\top M\begin{pmatrix}y\\x\end{pmatrix}$ (attained at $y=-A^\dagger Bx$), and $0\preceq M/A\preceq C$.
hypotheses: $A=A^\top\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$, $B\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$, $C=C^\top\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}$ (any `Fintype` indices, `Matrix.fromBlocks`)
$A^\dagger$ the Moore–Penrose inverse; no invertibility assumed
results.conclusion: $\mathrm{fromBlocks}(A,B,B^\top,C)\succeq0\iff A\succeq0\wedge(I-AA^\dagger)B=0\wedge C-B^\top A^\dagger B\succeq0$; and the variational identity for $x^\top(M/A)x$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Same criterion but requires A PosDef and [Invertible A].
Quadratic-form completion identity for invertible A.

results.notes: Gap with Mathlib: Mathlib's PosDef.fromBlocks₁₁ needs an invertible pivot; Nyström and Cholesky-type arguments have singular pivots (ΩᵀAΩ need not be invertible). Consumers: nystrom-structural (its 'A − A⟨Ω⟩ is the Schur complement' clause is recorded as not formalised), rpcholesky (the residual after k pivots is a Schur complement, hence PSD with trace decreasing), cholesky-decomposition (recursive step), nystrom-pcg, column subset selection / volume-sampling (Schur complements and determinants), Gaussian conditioning with singular covariance. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Löwner–Heinz and inverse antitonicity for real symmetric matrices
results.informal: For real symmetric $0\preceq A\preceq B$ and $r\in[0,1]$: $A^r\preceq B^r$ (in particular $A^{1/2}\preceq B^{1/2}$), and $A\mapsto A^r$ is operator concave on PSD matrices. If $0\prec A\preceq B$ then $B^{-1}\preceq A^{-1}$ and $\log A\preceq\log B$. ($A\preceq B\not\Rightarrow A^2\preceq B^2$; the range $r\in[0,1]$ is sharp.)
hypotheses: $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric, $0\preceq A\preceq B$ in `MatrixOrder` (Mathlib's Loewner order on real matrices)
$0\le r\le1$; for the inverse and log statements $A\succ0$
Powers via Mathlib's `cfc` on real symmetric matrices
results.conclusion: $A^r\preceq B^r$; $B^{-1}\preceq A^{-1}$; $\log A\preceq\log B$; $X\mapsto X^r$ operator concave on $\{X\succeq0\}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Löwner–Heinz for p ∈ [0,1], but in (complex) C*-algebras; Matrix n n ℂ is one only under the scoped instance Matrix.instCStarAlgebra. Real matrices are not a CStarAlgebra.
Real CFC on Hermitian matrices over any RCLike field, including ℝ.
Congruence preserves the order.

mathlib_prereqs.decl: Real-matrix transport of the CFC order results

results.notes: Mathlib has the full statement only for C*-algebras over ℂ; NLAlib's Matrix layer works with real matrices and `open scoped MatrixOrder`. The target is a transport: complexify with Matrix.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) (a star-algebra embedding that commutes with cfc and reflects ⪯), apply CFC.rpow_le_rpow / CStarAlgebra.inv_le_inv / CFC.log_le_log, and come back. Also note NLAlib.matrixLog_le_matrixLog and operatorConvexOn_neg_log (complex, Concentration layer) duplicate CFC.log_le_log / CFC.concaveOn_log; future work should cite Mathlib. Consumers: nystrom-structural and nystrom-pcg (A^{1/2} and inverse comparisons), sketch-and-precondition and ose-def ((1−ε)AᵀA ⪯ AᵀSᵀSA ⪯ (1+ε)AᵀA ⇒ inverse sandwich), leverage-scores (ridge leverage monotonicity), matrix-chernoff-sampling consequences, cg-convergence with preconditioners. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Condition number κ(A) = ‖A‖‖A†‖ and its characterisations
results.informal: $\kappa(A)=\|A\|\,\|A^\dagger\|$ for $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ (with the total conventions $\kappa(0)=0$); for $\operatorname{rank}A=r\ge1$, $\kappa(A)=\sigma_1(A)/\sigma_r(A)$, and $\kappa(A)=\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}$ for full column rank. Characterisations: $\kappa(A)\ge1$ for $A\ne0$; $\kappa(cA)=\kappa(A)$ for $c\ne0$; $\kappa(A^\top)=\kappa(A)$; $\kappa(A^\top A)=\kappa(A)^2$; $\kappa(QA)=\kappa(A)$ for $Q$ with orthonormal columns; $\kappa=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}$ for $A\succ0$; for square invertible $A$, $\min\{\|E\|:A+E\ \text{singular}\}=1/\|A^{-1}\|$, i.e. $1/\kappa(A)$ is the relative distance to singularity.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ (`Fin` indices for the singular-value forms)
Distance to singularity: $A$ square and invertible
results.conclusion: $\kappa(A)=\sigma_1(A)/\sigma_{\operatorname{rank}A}(A)$, the listed invariances, and $\min\{\|E\|/\|A\|: A+E \text{ singular}\}=1/\kappa(A)$
results.notes: NLAlib has NLAlib.frobConditionNumber (‖A‖_F‖A†‖, Kaczmarz) but no spectral κ; cg-convergence and Gaussian condition-number results state κ ad hoc. Define with the general moorePenroseInverse so it is total. Consumers: cg-convergence, sketch-and-precondition (κ(AR⁻¹) ≤ √((1+ε)/(1−ε))), nystrom-pcg, randomized-kaczmarz (relation κ_F ≤ √rank κ), linear-system-perturbation, least-squares-perturbation, pinv-spectral-tail (condition numbers of Gaussian matrices, cd05). Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Neumann series and perturbation of the inverse with explicit constants

mathlib_prereqs.note: ‖∑ xⁿ‖ ≤ ‖1‖ − 1 + (1 − ‖x‖)⁻¹; with ‖1‖ = 1 under the L2 operator norm this is the Neumann bound.
Only an asymptotic O(‖t‖) statement, no explicit constant.
Bridges Matrix ⁻¹ and Ring.inverse.

results.notes: A thin but much-cited wrapper: Mathlib has the abstract Neumann series in normed rings but no explicit, matrix-specialised perturbation bound in NLAlib's specNorm spelling. Proof: (A+E)⁻¹ − A⁻¹ = −(A+E)⁻¹EA⁻¹ plus the Neumann norm bound. Consumers: linear-system-perturbation, pseudoinverse-perturbation (square case), sketch-and-precondition, nystrom-pcg (regularised inverses (Â + μI)⁻¹), iterative refinement / sketch-and-iterate, T1 resolvent bounds. Recommendation: prove (quick win).

results.title: Normwise forward-error bounds for linear systems
results.informal: Let $A$ be invertible, $Ax=b\ne0$, and $(A+\Delta A)(x+\Delta x)=b+\Delta b$ with $\kappa(A)\frac{\|\Delta A\|}{\|A\|}<1$. Then $$\frac{\|\Delta x\|}{\|x\|}\le\frac{\kappa(A)}{1-\kappa(A)\frac{\|\Delta A\|}{\|A\|}}\Big(\frac{\|\Delta A\|}{\|A\|}+\frac{\|\Delta b\|}{\|b\|}\Big).$$ A posteriori: for any $\hat x$, $\frac{\|x-\hat x\|}{\|x\|}\le\kappa(A)\frac{\|b-A\hat x\|}{\|b\|}$.
results.conclusion: $\|\Delta x\|/\|x\|\le\frac{\kappa}{1-\kappa\|\Delta A\|/\|A\|}(\|\Delta A\|/\|A\|+\|\Delta b\|/\|b\|)$ and $\|x-\hat x\|/\|x\|\le\kappa\|b-A\hat x\|/\|b\|$
results.notes: Consumers: cg-convergence and nystrom-pcg (turning residual stopping criteria into error guarantees), sketch-and-precondition, randomized-kaczmarz / sketch-and-project error-vs-residual statements, iterative refinement with sketched preconditioners. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Wedin's perturbation bound for full-rank least squares
results.informal: $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ of full column rank, $x=\arg\min\|Ax-b\|$ with $x\ne0$, $r=b-Ax$. Let $\|\Delta A\|\le\varepsilon\|A\|$, $\|\Delta b\|\le\varepsilon\|b\|$, $\kappa(A)\varepsilon<1$, $y=\arg\min\|(A+\Delta A)y-(b+\Delta b)\|$, $s=(b+\Delta b)-(A+\Delta A)y$. Then $$\frac{\|x-y\|}{\|x\|}\le\frac{\kappa\varepsilon}{1-\kappa\varepsilon}\Big(2+(\kappa+1)\frac{\|r\|}{\|A\|\|x\|}\Big),\qquad\frac{\|r-s\|}{\|b\|}\le(1+2\kappa)\varepsilon.$$ First-order form: $\frac{\|x-y\|}{\|x\|}\le\varepsilon\big(\frac{2\kappa}{\cos\theta}+\kappa^2\tan\theta\big)+O(\varepsilon^2)$, $\sin\theta=\|r\|/\|b\|$.
results.notes: State the non-asymptotic Higham/Wedin form (explicit constants), mention the GVL first-order κ² tan θ form as the corollary people quote. Consumers: sketch-and-solve-ls (forward error of the sketched solution, not just the residual), sketched-regression, iterative sketching / Blendenpik-LSRN stability analyses, randomized-kaczmarz on inconsistent systems (kaczmarz-inconsistent). Recommendation: assume until pseudoinverse-perturbation is proved, then prove.

results.title: Cholesky factorisation: existence and uniqueness
results.informal: Every real symmetric positive definite $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ has a unique factorisation $A=LL^\top$ with $L$ lower triangular and $L_{ii}>0$; $L_{11}=\sqrt{A_{11}}$ and the trailing block of $L$ is the Cholesky factor of the Schur complement $A_{22}-A_{21}A_{11}^{-1}A_{12}$; $\det A=\prod_iL_{ii}^2$. Every PSD $A$ has $A=LL^\top$ with $L$ lower triangular and $L_{ii}\ge0$ (not unique in general).
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ symmetric positive definite (index `Fin n`, or a linearly ordered `Fintype`)
results.conclusion: $\exists!\,L$ lower triangular with positive diagonal and $A=LL^\top$; for $A\succeq0$, $\exists L$ lower triangular with nonnegative diagonal and $A=LL^\top$

mathlib_prereqs.note: S = L D Lᴴ for PosDef S (Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.LDL).
Lower-triangularity of LDL.lower is an explicit TODO in Mathlib's LDL file.

results.notes: Route: Mathlib's LDL gives S = L D Lᵀ with L⁻¹ lower triangular; finishing Mathlib's TODO (L lower triangular) and setting L·D^{1/2} gives existence; uniqueness by the usual triangular argument. Consumers: rpcholesky (partial pivoted Cholesky equals Nyström; residual is a Schur complement), nystrom-pcg (Cholesky of the core matrix), sketch-and-precondition (R = chol((SA)ᵀSA)ᵀ), qr-decomposition (R from AᵀA), Gaussian sampling N(0,Σ) = L z. Recommendation: prove (the TODO is a natural upstream contribution to Mathlib).

results.title: QR factorisation: existence and uniqueness
results.informal: Every $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge n$ factors as $A=QR$ with $Q\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $Q^\top Q=I_n$, and $R$ upper triangular with $R_{ii}\ge0$ (thin QR; a full QR has $Q$ orthogonal $m\times m$). If $\operatorname{rank}A=n$ then $R_{ii}>0$, the pair $(Q,R)$ is unique, $R^\top R=A^\top A$ (so $R^\top$ is the Cholesky factor of $A^\top A$), $QQ^\top$ is the orthogonal projector onto $\operatorname{range}A$, $\sigma_i(R)=\sigma_i(A)$ and $\kappa(R)=\kappa(A)$.
results.conclusion: $\exists Q,R$: $A=QR$, $Q^\top Q=I$, $R$ upper triangular with $R_{ii}\ge0$; unique with $R_{ii}>0$ under full column rank, and then $R^\top R=A^\top A$, $QQ^\top=AA^\dagger$, $\sigma(R)=\sigma(A)$
results.notes: Consumers: sketch-and-precondition (SA = QR, then κ(AR⁻¹)), haar-orthogonal (the Q factor of a Gaussian matrix with R_ii > 0 is Haar; needs uniqueness), rsvd-expected-error / hmt-9-1-spectral (Q = orth(Y); NLAlib currently uses polarFrame instead), leverage-scores (ℓᵢ = ‖Q_{i,:}‖²), block-krylov-lra. Recommendation: prove.

results.title: Subspace iteration as a sequence of subspaces
results.informal: The $k$-th subspace iterate from a starting block $\Omega \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times s}$ is the subspace $\mathcal{S}_k = \operatorname{range}(A^k \Omega)$; any orthonormal $Q_k$ with $\operatorname{range} Q_k = \mathcal{S}_k$ is a basis the algorithm may carry, and the Ritz pairs are those of $Q_k^\top A Q_k$. Orthonormalisation does not change $\mathcal{S}_k$, and $\mathcal{S}_k \subseteq \mathcal{K}_{k+1}(A, \Omega)$ (block Krylov with the fixed polynomial $x^k$).
results.conclusion: $\mathcal{S}_k = \operatorname{range}(A^k\Omega) \le \mathcal{K}_{k+1}(A,\Omega)$; the compression $Q_k^\top A Q_k$ is independent of the orthonormal basis $Q_k$ up to orthogonal similarity
results.notes: Design: the iterate is a subspace, every basis is a witness (docs/KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS.md §3.9). NLAlib already states the HMT power scheme on range((AAᵀ)^q A Ω) in LowRank/PowerIteration.lean; this entry names the object. Consumers: subspace-iteration-convergence, random-start-power, block-krylov-lra (comparison lemma S_k ≤ K_{k+1}).

results.title: Subspace iteration: tangent of the angle to the dominant eigenspace decays like (λ_{s+1}/λ_s)^k
results.informal: For symmetric $A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_n$, $\lambda_s > \lambda_{s+1} \ge 0$, dominant eigenspace $\mathcal{U}_s$, and $\Omega$ with $U_s^\top \Omega$ invertible: $\tan\theta_{\max}(\mathcal{S}_k, \mathcal{U}_s) \le (\lambda_{s+1}/\lambda_s)^k \tan\theta_{\max}(\operatorname{range}\Omega, \mathcal{U}_s)$, and per-vector: for each $i \le s$ with $\lambda_i > \lambda_{s+1}$, the angle between $u_i$ and $\mathcal{S}_k$ decays like $(\lambda_{s+1}/\lambda_i)^k$.
results.notes: Prove. Consumers: random-start-power (with the Gaussian a.s. invertibility of U_sᵀΩ and the tan θ₀ moment bounds), gap-dependent block Krylov comparison (mm15 §4), rsvd-spectral-expected with power iteration. Saad states the theorem for general diagonalisable A; the symmetric form suffices here.

results.title: Matrix-vector query model of an algorithm
results.informal: An algorithm with matrix-vector access is an interaction tree: it is either an output, or a query vector $v$ with a continuation that receives $Av$ (adaptively). Its cost is the number of queries; its semantics on $A$ is obtained by answering every query with $Av$. A randomized algorithm is a tree-valued random variable. "$x_q$ is computable with $q$ matvecs" means some tree of cost $q$ outputs $x_q$ for every $A$; Gram–Schmidt and other work not touching $A$ is free.
results.conclusion: A syntax `MatvecAlg n α` with `run A : α` and `cost : ℕ`; realisation theorems `∃ alg, cost alg = q ∧ ∀ A, run A alg = iterate` for Arnoldi/Lanczos, GMRES, CG and subspace iteration
results.notes: Design (docs/KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS.md §3.10): runtime statements at the level randomized NLA uses them. Upper bounds are realisation theorems; this is also the only setting in which matvec lower bounds (Braverman–Hallman–Musco 2020, Simchowitz–El Alaoui–Recht 2018) can be stated. Arithmetic cost (flops) is deliberately out of scope: recorded as notes on entries, not formalised. Consumers: every Krylov predicate (cg-convergence, gmres-def, arnoldi-def) gets a realisation theorem; lower bounds are future candidates.

results.title: Graded (nested) Krylov basis: unique up to signs, tridiagonal compression
results.informal: $Q = [q_0,\dots,q_{q-1}]$ is a graded Krylov basis for $(A,b)$ if it has orthonormal columns and $\operatorname{span}(q_0,\dots,q_i) = \mathcal{K}_{i+1}(A,b)$ for every $i$. For $q \le \operatorname{grade}(A,b)$ it exists and is unique up to the sign of each column; $Q^\top A Q$ is unreduced upper Hessenberg, and a Jacobi matrix (symmetric tridiagonal with positive-or-negative nonzero off-diagonal) when $A$ is symmetric. $Q_{q}$ is the leading block of $Q_{q+1}$ and $T_q$ the leading principal submatrix of $T_{q+1}$.
results.conclusion: existence; uniqueness up to $Q \mapsto Q D$ with $D$ diagonal $\pm1$; $Q^\top A Q$ unreduced Hessenberg, tridiagonal if $A = A^\top$; nesting of $Q_q, T_q$ in $Q_{q+1}, T_{q+1}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: one construction; the predicate is what theorems take

results.notes: Design: docs/KRYLOV_DEFINITIONS.md §3.11. The predicate, not the process, is what Jacobi-matrix theorems take; `arnoldiBasis` (positive subdiagonal) is one representative, and NLAlib's current `lanczosMatrix` with `lanczos_apply_eq_zero_of_add_one_lt` is the existing proof of the Hessenberg/tridiagonal part. Consumers: lanczos-recurrence, jacobi-matrix-identities, lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials, kaniel-paige-saad, finite-precision Lanczos statements.

results.title: Lanczos polynomials are the orthonormal polynomials of the spectral measure; T is its Jacobi matrix
results.informal: For symmetric $A$ and a graded basis with $q_j = p_j(A)\,b$, the $p_j$ are the orthonormal polynomials of the spectral measure $\mu_b$ ($\int p_i p_j\,d\mu_b = \delta_{ij}$), $\det(xI - T_j)$ is the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree $j$, and the entries $\alpha_j = q_j^\top A q_j$, $\beta_{j+1} = \|\,(A - \alpha_j) q_j - \beta_j q_{j-1}\|$ are the three-term recurrence coefficients of $\mu_b$: $T$ is the Jacobi matrix of $\mu_b$.
results.notes: Prove. The bridge between the Krylov module and quadrature theory: Gauss quadrature exactness (`lanczos-gauss-quadrature`) and the SLQ bounds become statements about orthogonal polynomials of μ_b. Consumers: jacobi-matrix-identities, lanczos-quadrature-*-error, spectral density estimation.

results.title: Jacobi matrix identities: Gauss nodes and weights, Christoffel–Darboux, continued fraction, interlacing
results.informal: For the Jacobi matrix $T_q$ of a graded basis: the eigenvalues $\theta_i$ of $T_q$ are the Gauss nodes of $\mu_b$ and $w_i = (e_1^\top v_i)^2$ the weights, so $e_1^\top f(T_q) e_1 = \sum_i w_i f(\theta_i)$ (Golub–Welsch); the eigenvalues of $T_q$ and $T_{q+1}$ strictly interlace; $e_1^\top (xI - T_q)^{-1} e_1$ is the $q$-th convergent of the Stieltjes continued fraction of $\int d\mu_b(t)/(x-t)$; Christoffel–Darboux $\sum_{j<q} p_j(x)p_j(y) = \beta_q\,(p_q(x)p_{q-1}(y) - p_{q-1}(x)p_q(y))/(x-y)$.
hypotheses: $A$ symmetric, graded basis with $q \le \operatorname{grade}(A,b)$, $T_q = Q_q^\top A Q_q$
results.conclusion: Gauss nodes/weights from the eigen-decomposition of $T_q$; interlacing of $T_q, T_{q+1}$; continued-fraction and Christoffel–Darboux identities
results.notes: Prove in pieces; each identity can be its own declaration under this id. Interlacing is Cauchy interlacing for the leading principal submatrix (`cauchy-interlacing`, proved), which is exactly why the nested (graded) basis is needed: the basis-free interface cannot state T_q ≤ T_{q+1}. Consumers: SLQ error analysis, Ritz value a priori bounds, spectral density / moment problems, Lanczos-based quadrature for log-det.

libraries.name: NLAlib (this repo)
libraries.scope: The library this atlas tracks. Layered modules Matrix → Concentration → Gaussian → Sketching → LowRank/Estimation/Krylov → Solvers. NLAlib/Concentration/Matrix/ is Tropp 2015 Ch. 3–8 (formerly the standalone TroppMatrixConcentration project, all Proved on Prove2me), reorganised by topic: Laplace, Series, Chernoff, Bernstein, Intrinsic, OperatorConvexity, Defs. Gaussian/ holds the ported Gaussian Random Matrices series: Concentration/ (integration by parts, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, log-Sobolev, Herbst), Comparison/ (Slepian, Sudakov–Fernique, Gordon minimax), Extreme/ (Lipschitz, Gordon, Chevet, spectral second moment, chi-square, small ball, deviation), InverseMoments/ (inverse Wishart, pseudoinverse tails), Moments/ (fourth moment, approximate multiplication).

libraries.name: Mathlib
libraries.scope: Upstream. Has stdGaussian / multivariateGaussian, HasSubgaussianMGF and the Chernoff-method sum bound, LinearMap.singularValues, the scoped Loewner order on matrices with CFC, Schur complements, matrix exponential, Gamma distribution. Lacks matrix SVD factorization, Eckart–Young, Weyl, Moore–Penrose, chi-square tails, any random matrix theory.

libraries.name: Gaussian Random Matrices I–III (Prove2me)
libraries.scope: Three-mission series in namespace GaussianMatrix on Prove2me (73 accepted solutions). Fully ported into NLAlib/Gaussian/ on 2026-10-09. The Wishart eigenvalue density bound gaussianMatrix_sigmaMin_transpose_sq_le_le_lintegral was historically an unproved Prove2me statement; it is now completed locally by the unshifted operator route. Kept for provenance.

libraries.name: LRA (Chen–Persson formalization)
libraries.scope: Local project (~/Documents/Papers/LRA-paper/formal). 253 theorems; RSVD, GN, tGN, etRSVD, etGN proved conditional on explicit Gaussian Props in LRA/Standard/Gaussian.lean.

libraries.name: HighDimProb
libraries.scope: External. Hoeffding, Bernstein, Hanson–Wright with explicit constant 1/(256e²) stated on Mathlib's HasSubgaussianMGF and iIndepFun, covering numbers, Dudley chaining, a Matrix Bernstein route, sample covariance. Pinned to Lean v4.29.1 and reported failing to build on v4.31–v4.33, so it cannot be a lake dependency of the Prove2me-pinned projects; treat as a proof quarry to port from.

libraries.name: AI4SLT (empirical processes in Lean)
libraries.scope: External, ~30k lines. Gaussian Lipschitz concentration via Gaussian log-Sobolev; Dudley entropy integral.

libraries.name: arlib
libraries.scope: External, 305 modules. Finite probability, concentration, Markov chains, coresets. No linear algebra.

libraries.name: OpenProblemsInNLA TR-01 companion (rerandomized SRHT)
libraries.scope: External. Prescribed-width subspace embedding theorem for a rerandomized SRHT, with kernel replay.

libraries.name: SparseStack OSE formalization
libraries.scope: External. Fixed-matrix theorem that fully independent SparseStack is an optimal oblivious subspace embedding. Repository URL not given in the abstract.

libraries.name: Finite-precision Krylov examples
libraries.scope: External. Exact rounding examples for CG/Lanczos; specific cases, not general theory.
